name: Prompt Vocabulary
description: A broad English image-generation vocabulary organized by functional category for agent-selected prompt construction. Entries include Danbooru and e621 tags and authored expressions, with concise descriptions of intended appearance and reported prompt use. Much of the usage knowledge follows the Japanese prompt dictionaries published by studiomasakaki on pixivFANBOX (the 2024 edition for AnimagineXL and NovelAI v3, and the 2025 edition for illustrious-family models), paraphrased in English; preserve any stated model scope. Definitions and usage suggestions help select vocabulary. They do not by themselves demonstrate that the selected checkpoint learned a term, that a weighting parser supports it, or that an output will realize its intended effect.

categories.name: Quality
categories.description: Terms naming requested fidelity, polish, detail, or a model's quality vocabulary. A definition describes the intended appearance or scoped usage, not a guaranteed model response. Actual output dimensions are chosen through generation controls.

categories.name: Negative Prompts
categories.description: Terms commonly used in negative prompts to discourage unwanted output characteristics.

entries.description: Negative with comic to stop the picture splitting into panels.
Negative against dreamy abstraction and stray patterns; usable in the positive too, and abstract background for the backdrop.
Negative cue against flat TV-frame screencap composition.
Writes the creator name in visible lettering across part of the image.
Negative for images with drawing mistakes.
A general negative that raises quality; combines with a part as bad face, bad hands, bad legs, bad feet.
Distorts the body with wrong proportions, misplaced joints, impossible bends, and mismatched parts.
Renders a poorly drawn face with muddy features, broken symmetry, and indistinct eyes or mouth.
Renders fingers with the wrong count, odd lengths, or bends that fold in impossible directions.
Draws hands with fused or twisted fingers, the wrong joint count, and shapeless palms.
Softens the entire frame so outlines and textures lose definition and everything looks smeared.
Cuts the composition off at the frame edge so part of the subject falls outside the picture.
Negative to remove the internal cut-in that explicit content often adds.
Prints a calendar date in small text, often in a corner like a camera timestamp.
Negative to remove a date written in a corner.
Renders mismatched or warped eyes with the wrong size, uneven placement, or unnatural pupils.
Warps the figure into grotesque wrong shapes with twisted limbs, melted features, and asymmetrical misplaced parts.
Renders limbs attached at wrong points or separated from the torso by a visible gap.
Negative for unpleasant images.
Shows glitchy rendering mistakes such as blocky patches, scrambled pixels, and broken geometry where detail should be.
Negative for images with too many limbs or digits.
Adds an additional finger or toe beyond the natural five on the hand or foot.
Adds arms beyond the natural pair, sprouting from the back, shoulders, or torso in odd positions.
Adds more than five fingers to a hand, often doubling digits at the knuckles.
Adds legs beyond the natural pair, duplicating thighs and calves in strange positions.
Negative for images with too few limbs or digits.
Reduces the finger or toe count below five, leaving a shortened or incomplete hand.
Draws hands or feet hovering beside the body with no connecting arm or leg at all.
Runs a strip of small text or graphics along the bottom edge of the image.
Runs a banner of text or graphics along the top edge of the image.
Draws an arm or leg with the wrong length, bend, or joint placement, reading as physically impossible.
Adds blocky compression squares, ringing around edges, and smudged color typical of a heavily compressed file.
Melts the fingers together into a soft dripping blob with no distinct separations.
Stamps a brand mark or emblem onto the image surface, usually small and high contrast.
Stretches the torso so the midsection appears unnaturally long compared with the limbs and head.
Elongates the neck far beyond natural proportion so the head sits unnaturally high above the shoulders.
Degrades the image with soft edges, washed out color, noise, and visible loss of fine texture.
Drops the resolution so edges turn jagged, textures flatten, and fine elements blur into coarse pixels.
Draws hands with warped structure, fingers bending the wrong direction or fusing together.
Negative for images with missing limbs or digits.
Omits one or both arms entirely, leaving bare shoulders or an empty gap at the sides.
Leaves one or more fingers absent so the hand shows too few digits.
Leaves an arm or leg absent entirely, ending in nothing where the limb should attach to the body.
Twists the hands into fleshy malformed shapes with swollen knuckles, merged fingers, and impossible angles.
As a negative it stops the camera pulling too far back; in the positive it leaves wide empty space in the frame.
Shows the small raised darker areola and nipple on an exposed breast, rendered plainly and anatomically.
Marks adult oriented content, typically showing nudity, explicit exposure, or sexual activity in the image.
Blurs the subject so edges dissolve and details smear into soft indistinct shapes.
Shows only a fragment of the face, the rest cut away by the framing or left unfinished.
Frames only part of the head, with the skull or jaw cut off by the image edge.
Sketches fingers as uneven wavering lines that merge, thin out, or trail off without clean edges.
Renders hands as sloppy sketchy shapes where the finger lines wander and the palm loses all structure.
Depicts natural hair growing across the pubic mound and groin on an exposed lower body.
Negative for raw-scan artifacts; fake scan in the positive for a poster or magazine look.
Negative for bleed-through and other scanning defects.
Adds a handwritten artist signature scrawled in a corner of the image.
Negative to remove onomatopoeia text.
Negative to remove speech bubbles, which comic and monochrome tags invite.
Presses a rubber stamp style mark with a border and lettering onto the surface.
Shows a smaller line of text beneath the main title or along the bottom edge.
Places readable or garbled lettering somewhere in the image, often as floating or printed words.
Displays a headline style title in large lettering across the image.
Distorts the subject with unbalanced features, uneven proportions, and a coarse unappealing look.
Distorts the facial features into an unattractive arrangement with uneven eyes, misshapen mouth, and poor proportions.
Negative against a half-drawn look; in the positive with sketch it becomes a style.
Prints an account handle in plain lettering on the image, usually near an edge.
Overlays a semi transparent identifying mark or word across the picture, often centered or tiled.
Produces a badly degraded image with smudged forms, murky color, heavy noise, and unreadable detail.
The low end of the aesthetic scale on Illustrious and NoobAI checkpoints, the counterpart of very aesthetic; in a negative it excludes renders the corpus rated poorly.
Pairs with worst quality in a negative to exclude the low-scoring slice of the training corpus.
Excludes the tell-tale texture of machine-generated images in the corpus: waxy skin, melted detail, incoherent ornament.
Excludes figures fused into each other where two bodies overlap.
Excludes hands and feet rendered with more than the expected number of fingers or toes.
Excludes anatomy that has grown into unrelated shapes.
Excludes faces and bodies with distorted features.
Excludes the corpus slice of images that carry untranslated foreign text: comic panels, captions, and signs.
Excludes wallpaper-format uploads: wide empty margins, centered logos, and desktop-sized compositions.
Negative against malformed feet with twisted toes, broken ankles, and wrong toe counts.
Negative against jagged stair-stepped edges on lines and curves; in the positive it yields a rough pixelated edge look.
Negative against limbs, joints, and bodies bent or attached in impossible ways; in the positive it yields deliberate comic body absurdity.
Negative against a squashed or stretched picture where faces and bodies look wider or taller than they should.
Negative against body parts drawn too large, small, long, or wide relative to each other, such as tiny heads or oversized hands.
Negative against mirror or water reflections that fail to match the figure above them in pose, clothing, or position.
Negative against dithered grainy dots and stepped color banding from a reduced color palette across gradients.
Negative against the off-model look of badly drawn animation frames, with wonky proportions, drifting eyes, and melting faces; in the positive it invites them.
Excludes the flaws of a scanned print: moire dot screens, paper grain, dust specks, color casts, and a dark band along a book's gutter.
Excludes the logo or address stamp of a gallery or wallpaper site laid over the picture, usually in a corner or along an edge.
Negative against misspelled or garbled lettering in any text within the picture; in the positive it puts a visible spelling slip into a sign or caption.
Excludes flat printed patterns such as plaid or florals that ignore folds and body contours; in the positive it gives a deliberately flat stylized print.
Excludes a website URL printed in a corner or along an edge of the picture as a signature or watermark.
Excludes the dark shadowed band, color shift, and blur along one edge that a bound book leaves when scanned without lying flat.
Negative against blocky macroblock compression and stepped color banding, the smeared look of a badly compressed video frame.
Negative against a visible seam or misaligned join where two pictures meet, with lines and colors failing to continue across it.
Negative against stray white specks and dust flecks scattered across the picture like a badly cleaned scan.

Smooth glossy white ceramic figures with painted detail.

Bold colour and structured strokes.
Loose design drawings for sets and props.
Heroic figures, bold slogans, limited colour.
Swirling lettering and vibrating colour.
Focus shifting between planes during the shot.
Lurid colour and heavy ink of mid-century pulp covers.
Coiled paper strips forming filigree shapes.
Unidealised everyday subjects painted plainly.

Balanced composition, sfumato, and classical figures.

Scratchy, satirical, deliberately crude comic drawing.
Blue-green submerged scenes with particles.

Pastel gradients, grids, statues, and glitch.

Darkened corners drawing the eye inward.
The faded tone and softness of an old photograph.

Colour and mood studies for animation.
Forms built from cubic voxels.

Watercolour softness without drawing the medium.

Very pale watercolour-pencil look; pencils appear more than with watercolor.
Clean digital comic drawing with flat colour.
American comic rendering, as against manga.
Soft bleeding edges where wet paint met wet paint.
Playful, fanciful drawing with gentle humour.
White lines on a dark ground.
A wide-angle look: broad view, stretched edges, exaggerated depth.
Accurate animal painting in natural setting.
Long-lens animal photographs.
3D shown as edge lines only.
Carved wood with grain and tool marks.
Fine white lines cut into a black ground.
Coarse black shapes and gouged white lines with wood grain.
Woven threads with a stepped, matte image.
Radial blur from a zoom made during exposure.
A pencil-drawn look with grey tonal shading and visible strokes.
A direct ink print of a fish on paper, showing every scale and fin in black ink with a hand-painted eye added.

Assembles the whole picture from a grid of hundreds of tiny photographs whose combined tones form the larger image when seen from afar.
Builds the whole picture from countless small dots of pure color that blend optically into forms and tones when viewed at a distance.

Yields rough storyboard-style frames with loosely sketched figures, minimal shading, and timing notes, like a pre-animation mock-up.

Gives the image a photochemical film look with visible grain, gentle color response, and slightly softened detail.
Removes color and renders the scene entirely through grayscale tones, contrast, and texture.
Combines Japanese anime character styling with comic-book ink outlines, graphic shading, and dynamic illustration.
Builds a comic-book image from deliberate hand-inked contours, hatching, and strong black-and-white contrast.
Combines animated comic forms with flat color, crisp ink outlines, and hard-edged cel-shaded shadows.
Uses the bold inking, dynamic anatomy, dramatic color, and panel-oriented rendering associated with Western comics.
Renders simplified, exaggerated cartoon forms as dimensional 3D objects with rounded volume and polished lighting.
Gives the image the appearance of a motion-picture frame through deliberate composition, dramatic lighting, and cinematic color grading.
Produces a polished, flattering portrait with controlled lighting, refined beauty styling, and emphasis on the subject's appearance.
Produces highly detailed 3D animation-style imagery with realistic materials, cinematic depth, and polished game-engine lighting.
Frames the subject as a vertical social-media video image with immediate visual impact and a casual, polished influencer finish.

Combines deep noir shadows and mystery with saturated neon light, luminous signage, and colored reflections.

Produces a technically polished photograph with controlled lighting, deliberate composition, clear focus, and refined tonal rendering.
Evokes older video-game graphics through pixelation, limited palettes, simplified geometry, or period-appropriate screen design.

entries.description: Fills the scene with organic grown technology, wet fleshy machinery, veins, membranes, and bioluminescent tissue.
Fills the frame with cathedral arches, stained glass, incense smoke, vestments, and gilded religious iconography.
Bathes a high tech city in neon signage, holograms, rain slicked streets, and glowing circuitry.
Reimagines the interwar era with riveted steel machines, soot, propellers, and heavy industrial machinery.
Pulses the scene with glowing club lighting, lasers, strobes, and abstract digital music visuals.
Mixes dark lace, corsets, silver crosses, and pale skin with torn black streetwear and moody lighting.
Applies traditional Japanese motifs, flat decorative composition, wave and blossom patterns, and calligraphic linework.
Shows a ruined world of crumbling buildings, rusted vehicles, drifting ash, and scavenged makeshift gear.
Melts the frame into swirling saturated colors, kaleidoscope patterns, and hallucinatory flowing shapes.
Renders sleek atomic age spacecraft, chrome fins, glowing energy rays, and retro science fiction futurism.
Imagines the future as past decades saw it, with chrome, tailfins, bubble shapes, and bright optimism.
Saturates the scene with aqua and teal tones, wave and dolphin motifs, and glossy ocean internet graphics.
Coats the scene in glossy translucent goo, dripping slime, bubbling fluids, and wet green translucency.
Fills the frame with worn spacecraft, starfields, asteroid debris, and rough lived in orbital gear.
Dresses the world in brass gears, copper piping, riveted leather, steam vents, and Victorian machinery.
Glows with magenta and blue neon, sunset grid horizons, chrome reflections, and eighties electronic energy.
Rebuilds the world with early electronics, vacuum tubes, exposed circuit boards, and chunky analog machines.
Washes the scene in pink and cyan gradients, marble busts, grid horizons, and eighties computer nostalgia.
Dresses the scene in ornate Victorian fashion, gaslight streets, horse carriages, and elaborate brass gadgetry.
Art deco styling.
Art nouveau styling in the Mucha manner.
A freezing setting with heavy clothing.
Meant as a cool mood; mostly adds heavier clothing and lowers colour temperature a little.
The rounded, wide-eyed style of American studio animation.
Elegance: full long skirts and gothic backdrops.
A fantasy setting; women tend toward princess styling.
Gothic lolita styling: black with red accents and pale skin.
A psychedelic, drug-vision mood.
Horror styling: ghosts, zombies, blood.
A picture built to frighten.
A slight rise in colour temperature; no hot-weather mood.
Cute: pink and light blue, ribbons and frills, a slightly younger subject.
Almost no background, a lone figure, and often no line art.
A forceful mood with weapons, monsters, and more red.
Cute with more dark purple and black and a shadowed expression.
Cute with more pale purple and pink.
The anime and illustration look of the 1980s: soft airbrushed shading, large glossy highlights in the hair, and muted film-grade color.
The anime and illustration look of the 2000s: crisp cel shading, saturated color, and pointed digital line work.
The look of late-1980s and 1990s Japanese PC games: a 16-color dithered palette, hard pixel edges, and flat backgrounds.
Dresses the figure in flowing layered skirts, loose peasant blouses, fringe, floppy hats, and stacked jewelry in earthy tones.
Colors the whole look in brown, cream, and pink like a candy box, with sweets motifs, ruffles, and chocolate-themed accessories.
A refined knee-length dress with a modest neckline, petticoat fullness, and muted florals or solids, worn with a bonnet or headdress in an elegant vintage look.
A softer pastoral take on the frilled petticoat dress, with gingham or fruit prints, straw hats, wicker baskets, and simple aprons.
Dresses the figure in shiny vinyl and reflective fabric, neon and UV colors, goggles, platform boots, and synthetic hair falls in a retro-future club look.
Pairs black clubwear with neon accents, synthetic dreadlocks, goggles, a respirator mask, and industrial straps and buckles.
Piles on hair clips, plastic toys, badges, and layered bracelets over bright mismatched clothes so every surface is covered in colorful accessories.
Dresses the figure like a flying celestial from cave murals, with a bandeau top, flowing pants, long trailing scarves, and gold and jade jewelry.
Mixes chains, mesh tops, striped sleeves, oversized band shirts, chunky skater shoes, and heavy winged eyeliner with dyed or split-color hair.
Puts the figure in tight black skinny jeans, a band tee or striped hoodie, a studded belt, and swept side bangs over heavily lined eyes.
Dresses the figure in fluffy pastel pinks, lavenders, and mints with tulle skirts, oversized sweaters, toy prints, and layered soft accessories.
Dresses the figure in a straight dropped-waist beaded dress with fringe, a bobbed haircut, a jeweled headband, long pearls, and T-strap heels.
A dainty feminine look of lace-trimmed blouses, ribbons, tea-length skirts, berets, and small chain bags in soft cream and pastel tones.
Dresses the figure in black lace, velvet, and leather with corsets, silver crosses, fishnets, and pale makeup with dark lips and eyes.
Puts the figure in a black leather jacket over a white tee, cuffed jeans, boots, and slicked-back pompadour hair, often beside a motorcycle.
Layers a flannel shirt over a faded band tee with ripped jeans, worn combat boots, and unkempt hair in a scruffy nineties look.
Mixes cute pastel outfits and plush mascots with blood spatter, bandages, eyeballs, and grotesque details for a creepy-cute look.
A tanned young man with bleached spiky layered hair, a slim open shirt or vest, tight pants, chains, and pointed shoes.
Floods the outfit with clashing rainbow and primary colors in loud prints, bright tights, and colorful accessories from head to toe.
Dresses the figure in nostalgic nineties and 2000s Japanese girlhood pieces like toy-print tees, colorful plastic hair clips, ruffled socks, and pastel charms.
A princess look with big teased curly hair, a pink and white lace dress with bows and roses, tiaras, and heavy doll-like makeup.
An extravagant princess dress with layered lace, roses, pearls, and a tiara over huge curled hair in pink, white, and gold.
A casual princess look mixing cardigans, tweed skirts, ribbons, and soft pink or beige tones with loosely curled hair and light makeup.
Dresses the figure in baggy jeans, an oversized hoodie or jersey, chunky sneakers, a snapback or beanie, and heavy gold chains.
Puts the figure in tie-dye, bell-bottom jeans, fringed vests, headbands, round sunglasses, beads, and long loose hair with flowers.
Dresses the figure in thick-rimmed glasses, a plaid shirt, skinny jeans, a beanie, and a vintage camera or record, often with a beard.
Blends a frilled petticoat skirt with a short cropped jacket-style top and long ribbon ties taken from Korean court dress, in pastel or muted tones.
Piles on rhinestones, leopard print, low-rise denim, velour tracksuits, big sunglasses, and chunky gold jewelry in a flashy 2000s look.
Dresses the figure in black or olive uniform coats with brass buttons, peaked caps, jackboots, and belts and straps in a strict martial look.
A frilled petticoat dress or skirt combined with a double-breasted uniform jacket, epaulettes, gold braid, and a peaked cap or beret.
Dresses the figure in a bright shift dress or miniskirt, bold geometric prints, a turtleneck, tights, go-go boots, and a sleek short haircut.
Layers loose natural-fiber dresses, cardigans, and lace in cream, brown, and forest tones with woolly socks in a soft fluffy woodland look.
Dresses the figure in a tight pencil skirt, a fitted blouse or blazer, narrow rectangular glasses, sheer tights, and heels in a sultry corporate look.
A boyish aristocratic look of knee-length puffed shorts, a frilled shirt with a cravat, a vest or short jacket, knee socks, and a small top hat.
Pairs black lace, crosses, and bats with pastel pink, lavender, and mint hair and clothes for a dreamy spooky mix.
Combines black goth staples like lace, fishnets, and dark lips with bright colors, playful prints, and a cheerful upbeat mood.
Dresses the figure in a polo shirt or oxford, a sweater tied over the shoulders, chinos or a pleated skirt, loafers, and a blazer with a crest.
Puts the figure in a studded leather jacket, ripped fishnets or plaid pants, safety pins, band patches, heavy boots, and a bright mohawk.
A frilled petticoat skirt in plaid or black mixed with safety pins, chains, studs, torn lace, striped socks, and a small top hat.
A frilled short dress built like a qipao with a mandarin collar, frog buttons, and brocade, worn with a petticoat and Chinese hair ornaments.
Dresses the figure in neon crop tops, fluffy leg warmers, beaded kandi bracelets stacked on the arms, platform boots, and glow sticks.
Sets the scene in early 1800s England with high-waisted empire gowns, bonnets, gloves, tailcoats and cravats, and drawing rooms or ballrooms.
Puts the figure in a polka dot swing dress with a red lip and victory rolls, or a bowling shirt, cuffed jeans, and a pompadour in a fifties diner look.
Fills the scene with pastel silks, wide panniered gowns, powdered wigs, gilded scrolling ornament, and flowers in an ornate 18th century salon.
A tanned girl with big bleached hair and dramatic makeup in black leather, plaid, chains, studs, and band tees with a rock edge.
Sets the scene in the 1830s with wide sloping shoulders, huge puffed gigot sleeves, full skirts, ringlets, and bonnets in a sentimental mood.
Puts the figure in bright neon skinny jeans, cartoon-print tees, lots of plastic accessories, and huge teased multicolored hair with striped raccoon-tail extensions.
A playful late-nineties Harajuku look of clashing bright colors, childish toy accessories, pigtails or buns, and layered mismatched pieces.
Dresses the figure in oversized hoodies, graphic tees, cargo pants or joggers, brand-name sneakers, and a cap in a trendy urban look.
A darker take on the pink and black jirai look, swapping frilly blouses for band tees, mesh, chains, and oversized streetwear in black with dyed hair.
A pastel knee-length dress bursting with lace, bows, and candy or animal prints over a full petticoat, with a bonnet and doll-like styling.
Dresses the figure in black technical fabric with many pockets, straps, zippers, and buckles, layered over skin-tight base garments in a functional look.
Colors the whole look in light blue and white with angel wings, halos, clouds, water motifs, pill and syringe charms, and glossy tech accessories.
Puts the figure in all black with heavy black eye makeup over white face paint, huge teased hair, fishnets, and ankh or cross jewelry.
Dresses the figure in peter pan collars, cardigans, knee-length skirts, tights, Mary Jane shoes, and quirky prints in a sweet vintage look.
Dresses the figure in shiny pastel metallic fabric, sixties space-age silhouettes, planet and alien motifs, and holographic accessories.
Sets the scene in 19th century England with corseted bustle gowns, top hats and frock coats, lace, gaslit streets, and heavy ornate interiors.
Mixes a long slit tunic or a wide-sleeved court robe with a frilled petticoat skirt, lace, and a flat round hat in Vietnamese-styled colors and motifs.
Dresses the figure in flamboyant gothic rock stagewear with heavy makeup, big dyed teased hair, leather, lace, and androgynous glamour.
Pairs a kimono or yukata top with a short frilled petticoat skirt, an obi bow, and lace, in a hybrid of Japanese dress and frilly fashion.
A childlike handmade look of mismatched bright colors, crafted felt and bead accessories, quirky prints, and playful DIY details.
Dresses the figure in low-rise jeans, baby tees, metallic and holographic fabrics, butterfly clips, tinted sunglasses, and chunky sneakers in an early 2000s look.
Mixes baggy pants, cropped tops, bold graphic streetwear, dyed hair, and piercings in a rebellious Chinese underground club look.
Fills the scene with dreamlike impossible imagery: melting or floating objects, mismatched scales, and things combined in ways that defy physics.
Draws the picture in a 1920s manner, with flat inky shapes, art deco lines, and period dress and hair.
Draws the picture in a 1930s manner, with soft rounded cartoon forms, heavy inking, and sepia toned color.
Draws the picture in a 1940s manner, with clean cel inking, muted color, and period hair and clothing.
Draws the picture in a 1950s manner, with bright flat midcentury color, bold outlines, and retro advertising shapes.
Draws the picture in a 1960s manner, with sharp pointed features, tall shining eyes, and flat poster color.
Draws the picture in a 1970s manner, with slender figures, huge sparkling eyes, feathered hair, and soft faded color.
Draws the picture in a 1990s anime manner, with hand painted cel shading, warm film grain, and period outfits.
Fills the frame with rave flyer graphics, warped chrome type, lurid gradients, and clashing layered stickers.
Blends African dress, pattern, and architecture with gleaming science fiction technology and cosmic color.
Breaks the subject into faceted geometric planes and reassembles them so several angles show at once.
Covers the design in thin sharp blackwork spikes and tribal glyphs with an occult cyber edge.
Bathes sleek futuristic forms in warm orange and red daylight with glossy highlights and clean curves.
Mixes glossy glass, water drops, and bubbles with lush green nature, blue sky, and clean 2000s interface shine.
Layers flat minimal shapes over swirling psychedelic vectors, glossy gradients, and bright bloom.
Sets stylish youth in a graffitied urban skate scene with street clothes, bold color, and Y2K futurism.
Imagines the future as the past pictured it, with rounded chrome machines, ray guns, and space age optimism.
Glossy girly 2000s fashion graphics built on stylized high heels, hot pink and black glitter, and leopard accents.
Blends East Asian and Pacific craft in silk, bamboo, paper, and lacquer with inventive retro machinery.
Fills the scene with sunlit greenery climbing bright buildings, solar panels, and airy optimistic architecture.
Flattens everything into glossy poster color with cheerful manga motifs that tip slightly into the surreal.
Turns nostalgic low quality snapshots uneasy, with dim flash light, odd empty spaces, and dreamlike distortion.
Presents a poised high-fashion figure in couture or editorial styling, with runway posture and polished professional grooming.
Creates a polished social-media influencer look with trendy clothing, careful beauty styling, and a posed lifestyle-photography finish.
Emphasizes an athletic physique through fitted sportswear, confident active posing, and a gym or wellness-oriented presentation.
Presents a polished beauty portrait with flattering light, elegant or figure-conscious styling, and an emphasis on allure.
Uses unconventional fashion and grooming such as dyed hair, tattoos, piercings, or subcultural clothing to create a non-mainstream look.
Dresses the figure in a distinctive heroic costume with elements such as a mask, cape, or emblem and reinforces the look with a powerful pose.
Presents a simply posed model against an uncluttered background with playful, suggestive charm directed toward the viewer.

Combines understated tailoring, neutral separates, and restrained accessories for an effortless Parisian fashion look.
Mixes leather jackets, band shirts, slim denim, boots, and metal accents into a polished but rebellious rock-inspired outfit.
Elevates relaxed everyday pieces such as jeans, knitwear, and simple shoes with refined fit, coordination, and accessories.
Blends athletic pieces such as track jackets and sneakers with tailored or fashionable separates for a polished sporty look.
Revives past-era silhouettes, prints, and accessories in a coordinated outfit that feels nostalgic but deliberately styled.
Combines cardigans, blouses, modest skirts or trousers, and glasses into a warm, bookish, neatly layered look.
Presents a fashionable urban look with current separates, practical statement accessories, and a confident metropolitan setting.
Uses impeccably tailored neutral clothing, fine materials, and discreet accessories without conspicuous logos to suggest inherited wealth.
Wears athletic staples such as leggings or joggers, hoodies, sports tops, and sneakers as comfortable everyday fashion.

Combines approachable casual clothing, soft natural grooming, and a reserved pose for an unassuming friendly look.

categories.name: Camera Viewpoint Directions
categories.description: Terms that specify the direction from which the subject is viewed.

entries.description: Strongly tilts the camera downward, looking well down at the subject from high above at a steep angle. Naming the surface the camera faces (floor) deepens the angle further and keeps the scene indoors; on tag checkpoints this reaches a steep look-down, not an orthographic top view.

Tilts steeply upward from a low vantage, exaggerating height and showing the underside of the subject. Naming the surface the camera faces (ceiling) deepens the angle further and keeps the scene indoors; on tag checkpoints this reaches a steep look-up, not a view from directly beneath.
Angles the camera downward from above so the head and shoulders dominate and the ground shows behind.
Positions the camera behind the subject, showing the back of the head and body with the face hidden.
Points the camera upward from below so the subject looms and the sky or ceiling fills the background.
Places the camera straight up beneath the subject, showing the underside with strong upward perspective.
Places the camera directly in front of the subject so the face and chest face the viewer square on.
Places the camera high overhead pointing straight down, compressing the body and spreading the floor around it.
Positions the camera to the side of the subject, showing the profile turned edge on toward the lens.
Shoots from above eye level looking down, making the subject appear smaller and revealing the ground around it.
Shoots from below eye level looking up, making the subject tower imposingly against the sky or ceiling.
Frames the scene from directly above looking down, showing the top of the head and the surrounding ground.
Composes from behind the character; a partial profile of the face often remains and the eyes may still turn toward the viewer. Facing away is the near synonym.
Camera at the height of the subject's eyes; the effect is slight and often not visible.
The frame stands in for a participant's own eyes.
A moderate look-down from diagonally above. Weight it and name the floor to steepen the angle toward a ceiling-height view.

A moderate look-up from diagonally below. Weighting the term and naming a ceiling are suggested ways to seek a steeper floor-level view; use a supported weighting parser and include a ceiling only when it belongs in the scene. Choose the camera position and direction needed for the intended low view in the selected input form.
Camera in front of the subject during an interaction.
Looks out from inside a room, vehicle, or other enclosure through a window or doorway at a subject outside.
Looks into a room from outside through a window or doorway; the character often appears peering out across the frame.
Composes from the side, like side view; add profile when a clean profile of the head is the point.
A low camera looking diagonally upward, close in effect to from below.
A shot past one shoulder from slightly behind. Alone it tends to be misread as off-shoulder clothing; combine with looking back or a back tag.
Camera behind the subject. Prefer this explicit form over a bare direction word attached to a body part, which can be read as a body region instead.
Composes from the side; a landscape canvas tends to give a profile head, a portrait canvas a bust, and the gaze stays forward unless directed.
Frames the character dead centre from the front, which pulls the pose toward left-right symmetry; use front view instead when a slight head tilt or other natural asymmetry is wanted.
A pose turned midway between straight-on and profile. The tag is weak on its own; pairing straight-on and from side across positive and negative can hold it.
The subject seen from behind.
Places the camera directly before the subject, showing the face and front of the body squarely.
Shows the subject's right side edge-on, reducing the face to a single clean profile.
Shows the subject's left side edge-on, reducing the face to a single clean profile.
Positions the camera on the subject's right, presenting the right side of the head and body across the frame.
Positions the camera on the subject's left, presenting the left side of the head and body across the frame.
Views the subject from between the front and right side, showing the face and the right plane of the body in a three-quarter composition.
Views the subject from between the back and right side, showing the back and right plane of the body while hiding most of the face.
Views the subject from between the back and left side, showing the back and left plane of the body while hiding most of the face.
Views the subject from between the front and left side, showing the face and the left plane of the body in a three-quarter composition.
Looks down from above the subject, emphasizing the top of the head or body and the layout of the ground below.
Presents an elevated aerial perspective with the subject set within a broad expanse of its surroundings.
Places the camera below the subject and looks upward, making the figure appear taller and more imposing.
Places the camera above the subject and looks downward, making the figure appear smaller and revealing more of the ground.
Positions the camera at the subject's eye height, producing a direct and naturalistic view without strong vertical distortion.
Looks steeply upward from near ground level, dramatically exaggerating the subject's height and the foreground perspective.
Looks directly downward from high overhead, turning the subject and setting into a clear top-down arrangement.
Rolls the camera so the horizon and vertical lines tilt diagonally, creating visual unease or energetic tension.
Looks past a foreground person's shoulder toward another subject, linking the two figures within the same composition.
Uses the camera as a participant's eyes, showing the scene as that person sees it rather than observing them from outside.

categories.name: Camera Angle and Perspective
categories.description: Terms for camera tilt and roll, perspective and foreshortening, viewpoint construction, projection, focus, and motion effects. These describe different properties of a view and can combine when they form a coherent picture.

entries.description: A steep view from high above, the ground filling the frame.
Defocused background plane; pairs with depth of field.
Near-plane defocus framing.
A view from directly below the subject.
The frame tilted off level, a dutch angle.
Composes with widescreen film style framing, shallow depth, and a deliberate dramatic camera placement.
A long lens flattening distance so far and near objects sit close together.
Strong perspective with lines converging far into the frame.
Focus falloff separating subject from background.
Composes from an extreme tilted or steep viewpoint that heightens tension and visual impact.
Pronounced apparent shortening of forms directed into picture depth, often with overlap. Aggressive enlargement of a nearer limb or projecting object can create a looming or reaching effect.
A high aerial view as from a drone, looking down or across.
Tilted camera roll for tension or energy.
A tilted horizon; the dutch angle.
The camera rolled so the horizon slopes.
Uses an energetic diagonal viewpoint with strong perspective lines that make the pose feel in motion.
The camera far below the subject looking sharply up.
Camera far below the subject, looking steeply up.
Exaggerated perspective with strong convergence and foreshortening.
The camera at the subject's eye height.
Meant as a view through spectacles, but in practice only adds glasses to the character.
Barrel-distortion wide lens look.
Warps the frame with extreme barrel distortion, curving straight lines and bulging the center outward.
Little depth; the scene reads as layers on a plane.
Scale tricks by placement: near objects made to read as large.

Apparent shortening of an object or figure directed into picture depth. The shortening can be subtle or pronounced; strong enlargement of a nearer hand, foot, or object is one possible perspective construction.
Curved, fisheye-like perspective with four vanishing points.
The subject seen square from the front.
The camera above the subject looking down.
A view from above the subject.
Framing that places the viewer inside the scene's space.
A forceful, dramatic camera angle; the expression tightens with it.
A parallel projection at equal angles, as in isometric game art.
Frames the subject small within a wide surrounding environment, showing the whole body and its setting.
A view from below the subject.
The camera near the ground.
Movement streak effect.
Compresses the scene with a tight telephoto view, flattening depth and isolating the subject.
Immersive viewer-position framing beneath the subject.
Lines converging to a single vanishing point ahead.
The frame past one person's shoulder toward another.
Frames the subject from behind a foreground shoulder that cuts into the near edge of the frame.
A view from directly above.
Emphasized depth perspective.
Depth conveyed by converging lines.
The frame as seen through a character's eyes.
Shows the scene through the eyes of a character, with their own hands or body edges entering the frame.
A side view of the face or body.

Two figures arranged in a rotated, yin-yang-like composition. Often fails, since inverting one figure is still hard; supporting tags such as circle formation, fetal position, sleeping, and on side help.
Composition cue emphasizing the subject's size against the frame.
Little depth; near and far compressed together.
A strict side view of the head.
The whole image rotated ninety degrees onto its side.
A high fixed camera's view, wide and impersonal.
The character faces the viewer in a mirror-symmetric arrangement; with two characters both fall into matching twin-like poses.
The subject turned about forty-five degrees from the camera.
The frame rolled off level.
A view straight down from above.
Lines converging to two vanishing points at the sides.
The figure inverted, head down and legs up. Renders more often as a flipped camera or a lying figure shot from the far side than as a handstand.
Explicit convergence-point perspective.
The position the picture is seen from; a general term that needs a specific angle beside it.
Captures a broad field of view with exaggerated perspective and space stretching toward the frame edges.
A wide field of view that stretches what is near the edges.
A view from ground level looking up.
Places the subject or viewpoint far above the ground, on a rooftop, cliff, or tower, with a long drop and a distant floor below.
Places the camera directly in front of the subject on a horizontal orbit, producing a square front view.
Places the camera diagonally between the subject's front and side, producing a three-quarter view.
Places the camera directly to one side of the subject, producing a side-on or profile view.
Places the camera diagonally behind one side of the subject, producing a rear three-quarter view with little or no face visible.
Places the camera directly behind the subject, producing a back view with the face hidden.
Places the camera diagonally behind the opposite side of the subject, producing the complementary rear three-quarter view.
Places the camera directly opposite the 90-degree side position, producing a profile from the other side.
Places the camera diagonally between the opposite side and the front, producing the complementary front three-quarter view.
Keeps the camera level with the subject, producing a straight view without upward or downward tilt.
Places the camera slightly above level and tilts it downward, producing a gentle high-angle view.
Looks downward from a moderately elevated position, revealing more of the subject's upper surfaces and surroundings.
Looks downward diagonally from above, making the ground and the tops of forms prominently visible.
Uses a steep elevated camera that emphasizes the top of the subject and compresses its visible height.
Looks sharply downward from nearly overhead, making the subject appear flattened against the surrounding ground.
Points the camera straight down from directly overhead, producing a top-down view of the subject and its layout.

categories.name: Subject Framing and Focus
categories.description: Terms that determine which part of the subject receives compositional emphasis.

entries.description: An arrangement read as shapes and tones rather than as a scene.
An animal as the main subject.
Compositional emphasis on the armpits.
Frames the buttocks prominently in close view, rounded and emphasized, often in tight clothing or nude.
Compositional emphasis on the buttocks.
Visual weight placed off balance across the frame on purpose.
Distance shown by haze, softening, and cooler tone toward the far ground.
Compositional emphasis on the back of the body.
Weight spread evenly across the frame; calm and stable.
The chest emphasized; cleavage for the cleft specifically.
The subject placed in the middle of the frame.
The subject in the centre of the frame with even margins.
Deliberately crowded and disordered arrangement.
Stresses the character over the setting.
Frames tightly on the chest, filling the composition with the torso and its clothing or skin detail.
Compositional emphasis on the chest.
Film-like framing: wide aspect, headroom and lead room by convention, deliberate light.
A plain, uncluttered background.
Frames tightly on the subject so the face or a detail fills most of the image.
A tight framing in which the subject or a selected detail fills much of the image.
A busy background full of objects and detail.
A picture whose purpose is the arrangement itself; often loose and sketch-like.
The frame's weights held in equilibrium.
Enough setting kept in the frame to place the subject in a scene.
The subject set into a corner of the frame with empty space opposite.
A couple as the main subject.
Frames the subject from roughly mid-thigh upward.
The arms are cut by the frame edge.
Parts of the subject cut by the frame edge on purpose.
Only the head within the frame; a weak tag.
The legs run out of the frame partway down.
Head to shoulder line only, as if floating.
The torso is cut by the frame edge.
Any device that shows depth: overlap, size change, haze, focus.
Foreground, middle ground, and background as distinct layers.
The main lines of the picture running on a diagonal.
Diagonal lines dominating the arrangement, giving movement.
Unposed, eye-level framing with the imperfections of a recorded moment.
Framing chosen for tension: steep angle, tight crop, strong diagonals.
An arrangement built on movement: diagonals, foreshortening, off-centre weight.
A background with nothing in it; the subject alone.
Fills the frame with one small region, such as a hand or an eye.
Compositional emphasis on an eye.
The face carries the picture, usually framed down to about the collarbones.
Frames the face so tightly that the eyes, nose, and mouth fill nearly the entire image.
Frames the face so tightly that the features fill nearly the entire image.
Compositional emphasis on the face.
The subject enlarged until it occupies the whole frame.
Objects arranged on a surface and shot from directly above.
One place in the frame where the eye is meant to land.
The feet or soles emphasized; feet focus is the same, leg focus for legs.
An object in the near ground giving depth.
The subject seen through or past a foreground shape that frames it.
The subject enclosed by a frame within the picture: a door, a window, branches.
Distance modifier that shrinks the subject within the frame; combine with a scenery focus for an establishing composition.
Frames the entire figure from head to feet with the whole body visible inside the frame.
Arrangement built on clear geometric shapes and divisions.
Placement by the golden proportion; a spiral or division of about 1.6.
Compositional emphasis on the groin area.
Frames the subject from the waist up, showing head, torso, and arms with the legs out of view.
Makes a hand or paw the subject of the frame.
Only the head is drawn, floating without a body.
The top of the head is cut off by the frame edge in a tight close-up.
Frames the head and shoulders.
A visible horizon dividing the frame.
Lines and weight arranged along the horizontal.
Movement suggested by pose, blur, or trailing forms rather than shown.
Close, quiet framing that puts the viewer near the subject.
A frame wider than tall.
Distinct planes stacked in depth.
Frames tightly on the legs, with the thighs, knees, or calves filling the composition.
Compositional emphasis on the legs.
Generous space around the subject.
Frames from the waist down, showing hips, legs, and feet while the upper half stays out of view.
Composition emphasizes the male character.
A mecha as the main subject.
A sparse, nearly empty background.
The subject framed by elements of the scene, such as an arch or branches.
Compositional emphasis on the navel.
Empty space used as a deliberate part of the arrangement.
Objects or still life as the main subject.
The subject placed away from the middle of the frame.
Elements running out past the frame edges; the picture continues beyond them.
A subject of unclear gender as the main subject.
Adult composition in which the explicit region falls outside the frame edge.
Arrangement and edges handled as in a painting.
Frames the head and upper torso closely, with attention on the face and expression.
A frame taller than wide.
Turns the subject sideways so only one side of the face and body is visible to the camera.
An explicit close framing on the genitals, uncensored.
Elements arranged around a centre, radiating outward.
A mirror or water reflection as the main subject.
The subject placed on the third lines of the frame.
The subject as a dark shape against light.
One character as the main subject.
Exactly one character in frame, no other people visible.
One character emphasized relative to other characters in the image.
The frame divided into two clear halves.
A square frame.
The subject separated from its setting by focus, light, or emptiness.
Mirror-balanced arrangement across the frame.
The subject framed with matched left and right.
Text as the main subject.
Thighs emphasized; zettai ryouiki for the skin between skirt and thigh-highs.
Very little space around the subject.
The frame held close on the subject.
Frames from the waist up, showing the head, shoulders, chest, and arms.
Composes the image from the waist upward, centered on the head, chest, and shoulders.
Lines and weight arranged along the vertical.
Pulls far back so scenery dominates and the character reads as a small figure.
One or more books as the main subject.
Garments as the main subject.
Clouds as the main subject.
Makes a nonhuman creature the main subject of the picture, framed and lit as the center of attention.
Frames the composition on the character's crotch, either by a close crop or by an angle that pulls the eye there.
Flowers as the main subject.
Shoes or boots, worn or set aside, as the main subject.
Compositional emphasis on the hair itself.
Compositional emphasis on the hips.
Makes large drawn kanji characters a central design element or the focal point of the picture.
A monster as the main subject.
Makes a mountain or a range of peaks the main subject, dominating the frame under the sky.
The mouth as the main point of interest.
Compositional emphasis on the neck and throat.
Compositional emphasis on the pectoral muscles, often in a close view.
Frames the composition on the male genitals with a close crop or an angle that centers them in the picture.
Plants as the main subject.
The sky as the main subject.
Centers the picture on the person being stepped on or trampled, with the foot or the other figure secondary to them.
The stomach as the main point of interest.
A tail as the main subject.
Makes a single tree the main subject, its trunk and canopy dominating the composition.
A vehicle as the main subject.
Centers the composition on one or more weapons, the blade or gun rendered as the main subject.
A hanging wind chime as the main subject.
Crops the picture so one arm runs out past the edge of the frame, the elbow or hand cut off by the border.
The eyes fall outside the frame edge.
One foot extends beyond the frame edge.
The knees fall outside the frame edge.
A character is cropped by the frame edge.
Crops the character down the middle so only one side of the face or body is visible at the edge of the frame.

categories.name: Shot Types and Views
categories.description: Terms for standard shot sizes and directional views.

entries.description: Frames the subject from mid thigh up, the classic western framing that leaves the gun belt visible.
Frames the face alone, filling the composition with the eyes, nose, and mouth.
Shows the subject turned fully away, with the back of the head and body filling the frame.
Faces the camera squarely, showing the subject head on in a symmetrical front facing composition.
Frames the whole figure from head to feet, with the entire body and its pose visible.
Frames the figure from the waist up, cutting the legs out of the composition.
Frames the head and shoulders closely against a plain background, centered like a formal portrait.
Looks straight down from above, showing the top of the head and the spread of the ground below.
Holds the camera at arms length in a slightly high tilted angle, close to the face with mild lens distortion.
The subject caught mid-movement; motion is the picture's point.
Head and shoulders to the chest; a portrait crop.
A close frame on the character's face and shoulders.
A close-up with film framing: wide aspect, shallow focus, directional light.
The frame cut tight around the subject with little margin.
A close framing of the subject, head and shoulders or tighter.
The top of the head cut off by the frame in a tight portrait.
The subject partly outside the frame.
Many figures filling the frame.
A shot of something other than the main action, inserted for context.
A close frame on one detail of a larger subject.
The subject far from the camera and small in frame.
One ear as the subject of the frame; an extreme close that leaves the rest of the head out.
A magazine-style picture: styled, posed, with a story implied.
The subject shown within a wide setting that says where they are.
A setting-first shot that explains where the character is; the character is tiny.
A very tight frame on one part: an eye, a mouth, a hand.
A very distant framing; the effect registers even if the distance is not extreme.
A very wide frame; the subject tiny against the setting.
A portrait framed on the face.
Fashion-magazine styling and framing.
The subject filling the frame edge to edge.
The whole scene shown, subject and surroundings.
Several people framed together.
The body from the head to the waist.
A portrait crop from the head to the shoulders.
The head as the subject of the frame, with the body cropped away.
A flattering, monumental framing of the subject, often low and centred.
High-fashion styling: poised, stark, editorial.
A short close shot of a detail cut into a scene: hands at work, an object, a screen.
A scene inside a room or building.
Extreme close photography of something small.
A very close frame on a small subject, with shallow depth.
A sweeping, scenic vista dominates the frame.
Framing from the chest up.
Framing from the knees up.
Framing from the waist up.
Renders the same character several times in one image from different angles, reference-sheet style.
A high vantage over natural scenery with the subject still properly drawn; the character usually gazes out at the view.
The camera swept sideways; the subject sharp, the background streaked.
A very wide field of view.
Only part of the subject shown.
A frame composed as a portrait of the subject.
First-person view at the moment a door opens: a character stepping through, or the room seen past the door. For a character looking in from beyond the door use peeking.
A clean, evenly lit frame of an object as in a catalogue.
The subject seen from the side.
Character reference sheet layout: full-body turnaround views, head studies, and often an automatic color palette on a plain background.
The subject seen in a reflective surface.
A wide framing dominated by the setting, close to wide shot.
One subject alone in the frame.
A portrait made under studio light on a plain ground.
The camera following the moving subject.
The body from the shoulders to the hips as the frame's subject.
The same character drawn from front, sides, and back in one image; pairs with reference sheet, multiple views, and variations.
Two heads close together filling the frame, as in a two-person close-up.
A wide arrangement with the subject small or spread across the frame.
A distant camera; the character becomes a small figure in a large setting.
Frames the subject fully visible but tiny within a vast surrounding scene, taking up only a small speck of the whole picture.
Frames the subject very small within a vast setting, making the surrounding environment dominate the image.
Shows the whole subject with generous surrounding space, preserving both the figure and its environment.
Frames the subject from head to feet so the entire body and its pose remain visible.
Frames the subject from about the waist up, balancing facial detail with gesture and some surrounding context.
Fills the frame with the subject's face or another important detail, excluding most of the body and setting.
Frames the subject from mid-thigh upward, the classic Western shot size that keeps a gun belt visible.
Uses a broad, setting-first view to establish the location and the subject's place within it.

categories.name: Gaze Direction
categories.description: Terms describing where the subject looks or how eye focus is directed.

entries.description: Pushing glasses back into place; brings a hand to the face but the gesture lands only sometimes.
Looking away awkwardly; blush and sweat tend to appear.
Leaves the eyes soft and blurred while other parts of the image stay sharp.
Turns the whole body toward the camera, front on, with chest and face oriented to the viewer.
Fixes the gaze on a distant point beyond the frame with a distant unfocused expression.
Gazing into the distance with the face slightly raised; adds a scenic feel.
Looking the way the body faces; pair with a body-orientation tag.
Eyes turned to one side without the head following.
Looking down at the own chest; the chest gets emphasized and the read is unreliable.
The gaze directed at another character in frame, not at the viewer.
Looking into a mirror, which appears; the reflection sometimes acts independently.
Eyes on a named object in the frame.
Eyes on the other character in a two-character scene.
Looking at a phone, which appears, with the gaze on it.
Eyes on the character's own body.
Directs the eyes straight into the camera, creating a locked engaged gaze with the viewer.
Directs the eyes off to the side with no eye contact, fixed on something outside the frame.
Glances over the shoulder toward the camera while the body stays turned away.
Turned away and looking back over the shoulder at another character.
Turned away and looking back over the shoulder at the viewer.
Drops the gaze below the frame, lowering the eyelids and tilting the head forward.
Eyes lowered toward another character.
Eyes lowered toward a shorter or lower partner.
Looking down at the camera; the expression tends to darken.
Replace {object} with the thing the subject is searching for.
Eyes straight ahead along the body's facing.
A composition of looking into a building, vehicle, or bag from outside rather than a gaze control; the gaze often returns to the viewer.
Looking out from indoors through a window, door, or veranda, often sideways; steer with other looking tags.
Peering over the top of glasses, which slide down the nose.
Turns the eyes sideways toward something off frame to the left or right.
Looking sideways; sideways glance for eyes only, averting eyes for an awkward look away.
Tilts the eyes upward toward something above the frame, lifting the chin and gaze.
Eyes raised toward another character.
Eyes raised toward a taller or higher partner.
Looking up at the camera; pairs with an angle tag, or split into looking down plus looking at viewer for better odds.
A back-arched turn toward the viewer, the so-called shaft angle; weak alone, so combine with looking back, arched back, head back, from behind.
The face turns quickly from side to side scanning the surroundings, often with motion lines or an afterimage.
The eyes drop to stare at a chest, the head tipped down toward it.
The eyes fix on an animal or fantasy creature sharing the frame.
The gaze drops toward a crotch, the head tilted down to it.
The eyes fix on one raised hand held up in front of the face.
The eyes fix on both hands held up and turned toward the face.
The gaze fixes on an exposed vulva in an explicit close view.
Bent fully forward so the head hangs between the legs, looking back at the viewer upside down.

categories.name: Ethnicity and Cultural Background
categories.description: Terms describing ethnicity, regional background, or culturally coded human appearance.

entries.description: Dresses the character in traditional African garments with beaded jewelry, bold patterns, and tribal ornament.
Renders the character with deep dark brown skin and African features.

Emphasizes numerous or strongly pigmented freckles, producing a densely speckled and highly visible skin feature.

Adds clearly defined indentations to the cheeks or other skin, producing readily visible dimples and small pockets of shadow.
Adds pronounced, deep indentations to the cheeks or other skin, producing strong dimples with distinct recessed shadows.

Adds numerous conspicuous pimples and inflamed areas, producing prominent acne across the affected skin.
Adds small scattered marks, slight discoloration, or tiny bumps, producing mostly smooth skin with subtle irregularities.
Adds realistic variations such as pores, small marks, and uneven color, producing skin that avoids a flawless airbrushed finish.
Emphasizes visible scars, bumps, discoloration, or other irregularities, producing strongly textured and conspicuously imperfect skin.

A flat hand waved in refusal, often both hands crossed in front of the chest to say stop.
Four fingers held up and spread apart with the thumb folded across the palm.
An old formal greeting with the torso bowed, one arm sweeping out low and the other tucked at the waist.
Both hands held open with fingers straight and palms shown, nothing hidden in either.
Thumb and middle finger pinched together with the other fingers curved out like orchid petals.
One fist tapped down into the open palm of the other hand, the gesture of a sudden bright idea.
Thumb and index finger brought almost tip to tip with a narrow gap left between them.
The little finger lifted away from the others in a dainty affected hold.
Thumb and little finger extended from a closed fist and shaken loosely in a surfer greeting.
The ring finger folded down to the palm while the other fingers and the thumb stay extended.
A finger or flat hand dragged sideways across the front of the throat as a silent threat.
Every finger splayed wide apart, each digit clearly separated from the next.
One or both arms thrust forward with the palm flat and the fingers pointing up, blocking the way.
One arm held rigid and raised at an upward angle with the palm down and the fingers straight.
A closed fist with the thumb jabbed downward in flat disapproval.
Both hands brought together with thumbs and index fingers meeting to frame a triangle.
Index and middle fingers raised into a V with the palm out and the rest of the hand closed.
A V of two fingers held up against the face so the eye sits between them.
A V of two fingers held across the lips, the mouth framed between them.
A raised open palm with the fingers parted into two pairs between the middle and ring finger, thumb out.
Three fingers held up and spread, or two fingers with the thumb out, reading as the letter W.
A hand lifted and swept side to side in greeting, sometimes with motion lines trailing it.
A hand raised to the head to straighten or settle a hat or other headwear into place.
Both hands raised to grip or hold the hat being worn, pressing it down onto the head.
A removed hat held against the chest in a solemn respectful gesture.
A hat held in the hand rather than worn, carried at the side or in front of the body.
A helmet carried in the hand or tucked under the arm instead of being worn.
A hand at the throat straightens or tugs a shirt collar or a worn collar into place.
Fingers pinch and straighten the ribbon tied at the collar, resettling its bow.
A hand fixes the knotted neckerchief at the throat, tugging the knot or smoothing its tails, on the wearer or on someone else.
Fingers lift or reposition a necklace at the collarbone, the chain or pendant caught mid adjustment.
A hand grips the knot of a necktie and straightens or loosens it at the throat.
Hands pull a scarf snug around the neck or resettle its wrap, on the wearer or on someone else.
A finger hooks the shirt collar and pulls it slightly down or away from the neck, a flustered or overheated gesture.
Both hands raised to clasp or cradle the own throat, elbows lifted and the face framed between the forearms.
A hand clutches a scarf while it is being worn, tugging or adjusting it at the neck.
Both arms thrown straight up and out in a V of joy, the body forming the shape of the emoticon.
Both arms spread straight out to the sides like wings, usually while running or in motion.
One arm extended straight out and the other drawn back bent at the elbow, the head turned along the extended arm as if aiming a bow.
One arm hangs relaxed at the side of the body while the other arm does something else.
One arm raised and bent so the hand rests behind the head, elbow pointing out.
A rude gesture with one forearm raised bent at the elbow while the other hand slaps or grips the crook of that arm.
An object or a person tucked and carried under one arm, held snug against the side of the torso.
Holds both arms up with the elbows bent and the wrists limp, hands dangling in front of the body like a cartoon ghost.
Sets one arm up behind the head while the other hand rests on the hip, usually with the weight cocked to one side.
Extends one arm straight out away from the body while the other stays lowered or relaxed.
Both hands mirror the same gesture, held at matching heights on either side of the body.
One hand reaches across to rest on the figure's own shoulder, the arm folded over the chest.
Both hands come up to rest on the figure's own shoulders, arms crossed over the chest.
An object carried slung or balanced over one shoulder, steadied there by a raised hand.
A sword laid back across one shoulder, the blade angled up behind the head.
A hand reaching back to clutch the figure's own wing, fingers closed around a feathered or membranous edge.
A pose with both of the figure's hands placed behind the head, bending the elbows and opening the upper body.

entries.description: A pose with both hands placed lightly on the thighs.
A pose with the figure's own hands clasped together, with the fingers wrapped or interlocked.
A pose with the hands held close to the face without specifying contact.
A pose with the hands raised to touch the hair.
A pose with fingers woven between other fingers, either within the figure's own hands or with another person's hand.
A pose with the fingers closed firmly around an object or other held element.

categories.name: Multi-Subject Poses
categories.description: Terms for contact, arrangement, and interaction among multiple subjects.

entries.description: An adult holds an infant securely against the chest or hip, supporting its head.
An arm around a partner's shoulders.
An arm around a partner's waist.
One figure's arm drapes around the other's shoulders or waist in a loose half embrace.
Two characters with buttocks touching; adult models tend to give a side-by-side rear comparison, so add back-to-back for a true back-to-back.
Carrying someone like a baby; without attributes an actual baby appears.
Two figures stand pressed spine to spine, facing in opposite directions.
Two characters belly to belly; rare and failure-prone.
A chest resting on a carried object; state carrying and the object.
One figure bears another's full weight in the arms while standing or moving.
One figure slings another limply across the shoulders, head hanging down the back.
A cheek resting on another's chest; fails without detailed tags.
An adult supports a child against the hip or chest, holding the legs steady.
A huddle circle; enough people that each breaks, and some models draw a stray circle instead.
Each arm hugged by a different character; pair with girl sandwich.
Kissed on both cheeks by two characters; pair with girl sandwich.
Exactly two characters in frame as the paired focus.
Two figures lock gazes directly, eyes meeting across the space between them.
Two figures oriented toward one another, with their faces directed at each other.
A person carried across both shoulders.
A button popping off a strained shirt; unreliable.
Two figures lean in until their foreheads touch, eyes often gently closed.
A character flanked by two girls; boy sandwich and boy and girl sandwich exist too.
Three or more characters together in one frame.
Three or more figures pile into one embrace with arms overlapping around each other.
A head resting on another's chest; hard to read unless the other face is in frame.
Two figures lean their heads until they touch, temple to temple.
Stresses a height gap between characters; random but effective.
Two figures link hands, fingers intertwined or clasped between their bodies.
Two figures embrace with arms wrapped around each other and bodies pressed close.
One figure wraps both arms around another from the rear, chin over the shoulder.
A shorter figure embraces a taller one with the cheek resting against the breast.
One figure embraces another with the head resting against the other's chest.
Two pairs of fingers weave tightly together, knuckle pressed against knuckle.
A head resting in another's lap; hair spread out draws the sleeper's hair, and closed eyes or eye contact sets the gaze.
Legs wrapped around a partner in a face-to-face embrace; limbs tangle and fail, and in adult context it becomes mating press.
Several characters in a row; queue for a line front to back, side-by-side to stress shoulders together facing one way.
Several figures lie on the ground with their heads gathered toward a shared center.
Two or more boys or men in frame together.
Two or more girls or women in frame together.
Two chests touching nipple to nipple.
Two faces lean so close that the tips of their noses brush together.
One figure lies draped across another's lap with the bottom raised, often for a spanking.
A bra far too large.
Carrying someone on the back.
One figure cradles another horizontally in both arms against the chest.
Characters lined up front to back, usually a loose cluster.
A smaller figure rides clinging to the top of a larger one's shoulders.
Shoulders touching; unstable, pair with symmetrical docking or facing viewer.
Characters side by side, mainly two; lineup for three or more.
One figure sits squarely on the other's lap, legs draped to one side.
One figure perches their weight on another's lap, chest, or back.
Two figures sit pressed together on the same surface with shoulders touching, facing the viewer.
A tiny figure standing on a giant's shoulder; needs an extreme size gap, weak.
Two characters pressed together in mirror symmetry; state who and where (2girls, couple, cheek to cheek) or it fails.
Two figures press their cheeks together side by side in mirrored poses.
Two figures stand mirrored with their fronts pressed flat together from chest to hips.
A shorter figure rises onto the toes to reach the other's lips for a kiss.
Arms circle snugly around the other figure's waist, pulling the bodies together.
Weighing the chest on a scale.
One character's teeth close gently on another's ear, the head leaned in close.
A tongue extends to lick along the rim of another character's ear.
Two characters wearing each other's glasses, the swapped pairs clearly mismatched to their faces.
Two characters making matching hand signs together, their gestures joined into one shape.
Four characters leaning in so their hands meet and build a single heart between them.
Two characters curling their tails together so the tips form one heart between them.
One character pins another head still and grinds a knuckled fist against the scalp.
Several characters touching fingertips so their hands together outline a five pointed star.
A group of characters all shown in side profile, lined up facing the same direction and often looking straight ahead.
One figure's arm hooks around the back of another's neck, pulling the two close together.
Both arms wrapped behind a partner's neck with the hands meeting at the nape, usually in an embrace or a kiss.
One character's teeth close on another's neck, the head bent to the throat in a vampire bite or an intimate nip.
Both of one character's hands rest on a partner's neck, reading as tenderness, fastening a necklace, or a threat depending on the faces.
One character presses lips to a partner's neck, head tucked below the jaw while the partner tilts away to expose the throat.
One character's hand seizes the ribbon tied at a partner's neck and pulls, tugging them closer.
One character's hand grips a partner's knotted neckerchief and tugs it, pulling their faces closer.
One character grips a partner's tie, ribbon, or collar and yanks them in, faces pulled close.
One long scarf wrapped around the necks of two characters at once, tying them together in an affectionate pose.
Two characters stand or kneel back to back with their rears pressed together.
One figure kneels on all fours while another sits down on their back as if it were a stool.
Two figures hook their arms through each other at the elbow, the inner elbows pressed directly together.
Two figures stack, one gripping the other's legs while the upper one balances on them with both arms stretched out like a cactus.
One figure sits perched on top of another figure's head.
A tail wraps around a partner's torso and pulls them in close against the body.
One figure sits astride a single thigh of another, hips settled down onto it.
Large wings fold forward around a figure and gather them in like a pair of encircling arms.
A small animal perched on the figure's shoulder, settled in against the neck.
One figure lays a whole forearm across another's shoulder, leaning a little weight onto them.
A bird perched on the figure's shoulder with its claws gripping the cloth.
A cat perched on the figure's shoulder, draped against the side of the head.
A small fantasy creature riding along on the figure's shoulder.
A small dog carried up on the figure's shoulder, held in against the neck.
Both hands rest together on one single shoulder of another figure.
Both hands rest on another figure's shoulders, one on each side.
A rabbit perched on the figure's shoulder with its ears up beside the head.
Hands knead another figure's shoulders from behind, thumbs pressing into the muscle.
One figure's hand clenched around another figure's wing, gripping the feathers or membrane and pulling on it.
A hand resting flat on another figure's wing, touching the feathers or membrane gently without gripping.
A figure gripping a partner's wings and holding them steady, usually both hands wrapped around the wing bases from behind.
Two figures wrap their arms around one another in a close hug, making affection or comfort visible through direct body contact.
usage_notes: Source: https://e621.net/wiki_pages/hug; e621 aliases hugging to hug.

entries.description: Two figures press their lips together, or one presses their lips to the other's cheek or body, creating an affectionate focal gesture.
usage_notes: Source: https://e621.net/wiki_pages/kissing.

entries.description: Two figures hold one another in their arms, producing a close affectionate pose with contact around the shoulders, back, or waist.
usage_notes: Source: https://e621.net/wiki_pages/hug; e621 aliases embracing to hug.

entries.description: Two figures lie in close body contact with at least one wrapped around the other, creating an intimate pose of affection or comfort.
usage_notes: Source: https://e621.net/wiki_pages/cuddling.

entries.description: Two figures combine a close embrace with a kiss, producing an especially affectionate pose with both arm contact and lips meeting.
Two figures coordinate their bodies in a shared dance, creating a sense of rhythm and partnership through their connected or mirrored movement.
One figure leans close to whisper into another's ear, producing an intimate or secretive interaction with their heads near together.
Two figures face one another and meet each other's gaze, creating a direct emotional connection across the space between them.
Two figures exchange playful teasing through amused expressions and light gestures, producing a lively friendly or flirtatious interaction.
Two figures lean together in a confidential exchange, often with one speaking quietly and the other listening closely.
Two figures softly place their hands on one another's cheeks or jaws, creating a tender close-range interaction.
Two figures lean until their heads rest against one another, producing a quiet pose of closeness and trust.
Two figures encircle one another with their arms, creating a mutual close hold around the shoulders, backs, or waists.
Two figures dance closely at an unhurried pace, producing an intimate coordinated pose with gentle steps and held hands or embraced bodies.
Two figures share visible laughter through open smiles and animated body language, creating a joyful social moment.
Two figures share an affectionate pause through close proximity, tender expressions, and attentive body language, creating a romantic mood.
Two figures look at one another with warm affectionate expressions, making their emotional connection the focus of the image.
Two figures draw their bodies near and hold one another securely, producing an intimate protective embrace.
