Sadness and warmth together; smile with wet eyes.
Fear present and overridden; forward step despite tension.
Frustration at an outcome that cannot be changed; clenched restraint.
Deliberate calm under circumstance; level gaze, controlled stillness.
Looking down on another; raised chin, half-lidded dismissal, sneer.
Attention pulled toward something new; head tilt, forward ears, raised brows.
Belief that nothing will change; collapsed posture, vacant eyes.
Bearing that claims standing; lifted chin, squared shoulders.
Rejection of something offensive; recoil, wrinkled muzzle or nose, turned head.
Falling short of expectation; flat mouth, withdrawn engagement.
Feeling absent where feeling is expected; neutral features, unfocused stare.
Wanting what another has; fixed watching, tightened mouth.
High positive arousal; forward lean, brightened eyes, quickened movement.
Waiting for something believed to be coming; forward attention, held breath.
Pleased surprise at good luck; disbelieving smile.
Pleasure at another's misfortune; asymmetric smile, leaning in to watch.
Warm acknowledgement directed at someone.
Pleasure from having done right; quiet settled satisfaction.
Knowledge of having caused harm; braced shoulders, unmet gaze.
Simple positive feeling; lifted features, relaxed frame.
Sustained hostility toward someone; fixed cold intensity.
Belief that something better is possible; lifted gaze, opened chest.
Restless urgency; shifting weight, tapping, clipped movement.
Ranking oneself below another; shrunken posture, upward glances.
Fear of losing someone to a rival; possessive orientation, hardened stare.
Directed drive toward a goal; forward weight, fixed target gaze.
Struck by something meaningful; stilled breath, brimming eyes.
Committed lethal intent; flattened affect, locked target, absolute stillness before motion.
Failed expectation; furrowed brow, tilted head, arrested motion.
Wishing an action undone; averted gaze, slumped line.
Low tension throughout; loose joints, slow breath.
Long-carried grievance; controlled surface over hardened core.
Struggle abandoned; dropped shoulders, released tension, flat gaze.
Deference toward another; lowered intensity, attentive orientation.
Weight of duty accepted; steady jaw, grounded stance.
Sufficiency reached; released tension, settled breath.
Settled, unthreatened; open posture and unguarded gaze.
Interest with an erotic charge, still exploratory rather than committed.
Grief; heavy frame, downturned features, slow movement.
Ongoing pain, physical or emotional; braced body, strained features.
Ranking oneself above another; expansive posture, looking down.
Careful gentleness toward someone; softened hands, quieted voice.
Held readiness; locked joints, raised guard, shortened breath.
Grievance turned to intent; narrowed focus on the target.
Fond ache for something distant or lost; soft distant gaze, faint smile.
Wanting something out of reach; reaching orientation, unfocused middle distance.
A menacing presence: narrowed eyes, a level stare, and a posture that reads as a threat.

categories.name: Composition Formats
categories.description: Layouts and presentation formats a picture can take: standing character art, sheets, cards, covers, screenshots, photo props, and scene-in-water framings.

entries.description: A period art style; 1990s_(style) and similar work the same way, and some models add their own era tags such as newest or oldest.
A frozen-instant dramatic shot; no effect on illustrious-family models.
The character floating on the water surface.
A held phone screen showing the character behind it; does not work alone.
Card styling on a portrait canvas; on other canvases a physical playing card appears.
A character explanation sheet with a main figure surrounded by text and face variations; highly random.
A composition assembled from distinct image, paper, drawing or lettering fragments. Crop, overlap, scale and spacing establish their selected relationships.
Several bordered character panels of equal size lined up in a row or column, a group-picture format.
Book or magazine cover styling; magazine cover or dojin cover sharpens it.
Body-pillow art: a character lying on sheets with a suggestive expression; pairs with on back, bed sheet, lying.
Dust and fragments hanging in the air for a tense atmosphere; dust cloud for smoke-like haze.
A cloud of dust, including the comic scuffle cloud.
A framed expression-challenge grid of front-facing faces; more usable than expressions.
A set of the same character's expressions; on illustrious-family models it floods the canvas.
App-style doodles on the face; weak, use drawn tags instead.
A phone camera screen with black bars and a shutter button; use a portrait canvas and negative phone if a handset appears.
A photo-like picture, often with a white polaroid border or placed on a desk, and a snapshot pose; pushes the subject toward photorealism.
An authored image adopting a selected game, stream or application capture format. Interface elements, wording and legibility follow the intended screen state.
A collectible figure appears, often the character rendered as one or a figure inside the scene; a character on a cut-out scenery base is faux_figurine.
Diving underwater without equipment; specify pose and placement.
A group picture of three or more characters.
A two-panel before-and-after adult comic format; needs a landscape canvas and adult tags to land.
A sitting pose with nothing drawn under the character.
A leaning pose with no wall drawn; low success on illustrious-family models.
An isometric illustration of buildings or a town seen from diagonally above with the character in it; diorama for a cut-out scene, dollhouse view for a room plan.
Reads as collage rather than a magazine page: cut-and-paste assembled illustrations.
A designed publication cover organizing a masthead, lead image, and any required cover lines. Wording, legibility, and image prominence follow the intended cover.
A phone selfie in a mirror; the character may spill past the mirror edge, so pair with holding phone and reflection focus.
A mosaic-tiled background rather than a mosaic of the whole picture.
A motion-filled shot similar to 1ms shutter speed; no effect on illustrious-family models.
A striking, designed movie-poster layout.
The camera half submerged, showing above and below the waterline at once; may sink entirely, so steer with canvas size, sky, or cowboy shot.
A physical photograph inside the picture, hung on a wall or held.
A frame around the whole picture, or a framed picture hanging on a background wall.
Instant-photo styling with a wide white bottom border; white border strengthens it, and negative character signature or text if a signature appears.
Photo-booth sticker styling; weak, and drawn doodles come better from drawn tags.
Rubble on the ground; ruins for a ruined building.
The character seen in a mirror looking back at the viewer; may spill past the mirror edge.
Feet dipped in water, usually barefoot.
Part of the body in water, as in a hot spring; alone it may submerge everything, so specify pose and placement.
A standing character illustration, usually a natural front-facing full figure; can drift toward game character art and is somewhat unstable.
A photo being taken, with the character posing for the camera; negative viewfinder or fake phone screenshot if a capture overlay appears.

entries.term: three views from front back and side
entries.description: The same character drawn from three directions.
A collectible card face organizing artwork with selected identifiers or game information. Orientation, frame, symbols and wording follow the intended card design.
A camera viewfinder overlay with battery and REC marks.
A four-panel vertical comic strip. In a negative it removes panel layouts and gutters.
A decorated border drawn around the whole image, as on a framed print or an old portrait.
A lace pattern running along the edges of the image as a frame.
A composition mirrored across a central axis; faces, poses, and backgrounds line up left and right.
Yields a head to toe outfit showcase, the figure posed to display a coordinated on-trend ensemble.
A grid of thirty five small portraits of one character, each head carrying a different expression.
A sheet of one character repeated through a set of twelve expressions, from blank and smiling to crying.

entries.term: hurt expressions of your wife practice
entries.description: A sheet of one character repeated through a range of hurt, pained and tearful expressions.
The same character repeated in several small portraits, each one carrying a different expression.
A sheet of one character repeated through a set of mildly lewd, flushed and teasing expressions.
A single self-contained comic panel with a border, holding the whole gag or scene in one frame with a caption or balloon.
A comic strip of three bordered panels in a continuous vertical or horizontal run, reading a short scene in three beats.
A comic strip of five bordered panels in a continuous vertical or horizontal run, reading a short scene in five beats.
Music-release cover artwork organized for a compact cover field. Artist wording, title, and purely visual treatment depend on the intended design.
A glossy commercial photo card portrait of a performer, posed and lit like a studio publicity photo, in a collectible print.
Lays the picture out as a calendar page, with a month name and a grid of dates printed beside or beneath the artwork.
Frames the picture as a music CD cover devoted to one character, with the character large and a song title and name over the art.
Arranges the picture as an organized grid or lineup of labeled figures or panels for side by side comparison.
The front design of a publication, using an image, typography, or both to establish its identity.
Inserts a smaller picture, often a face or a pair of eyes in close-up, cutting across the main image inside its own framed strip.
Lays out symbols, arrows, and short labels to show a flow of steps or connections, such as a relationship map.
A miniature scene enclosed in a box or set on a small cut-out base, with props building a partial background around the figures.
Cover artwork for a self-published comic or other fan publication. Title, creator information, and rating marks appear when part of the selected design.
A home-video sleeve design whose front, spine, back, and printed information depend on the intended view of the object or artwork.
Edges the picture with a border that dissolves gradually into the image instead of stopping at a hard line.
Frames the picture as a mock-up magazine, comic, album, or game cover, with invented titles and blurbs laid over the art.
Adds a drawn vertical scrollbar along the edge, suggesting the picture continues below the visible area.
Restages a famous painting's composition and palette with the characters swapped in, mimicking the classical or modern original.
Renders the picture as a video game screen capture, with health bars, menus, dialogue boxes, or other interface overlaid.
A small simplified square image of a program or file, flat and bold with a rounded frame, as it appears on a desktop or taskbar.
A picture captioned with bold white block capitals outlined in black at the top and bottom, in the classic internet meme layout.
A thin one or two line border drawn inside the picture, clearly set in from the outer edge as a frame within the frame.
Adds black bars across the top and bottom of the picture, narrowing it to a wide cinematic strip.
Cover artwork for a manga volume, balancing the lead imagery with any required title and publication information.
Lays out a fighting-game style sheet of one character repeated in several attack poses, each with a label or input notation beside it.
Puts two or more four-panel vertical comic strips side by side in one picture, each strip a separate short gag read top to bottom.
Divides the picture into several sections, each rendered entirely in a single different hue, so the parts read as tinted panels next to each other.
Yields a polished promotional wallpaper layout: characters posed against a wide clean background with open space left for a logo and desktop icons.
Adds a small bonus strip or side illustration beside or after the main piece, drawn looser and more casual than the work it accompanies.
Lets a character or object spill over the frame, letterbox bars, or panel edge that contains the rest of the picture, breaking out of the border.
A drawn character cut out of paper and photographed propped up in a real-world setting, its flat cartoon surface contrasting with the photo around it.
Lays the picture out as a small credit-card sized collectible card, with the illustration filling the card face beside a value mark or logo strip.
Puts solid vertical bars down the left and right sides of the picture, leaving a narrower upright image in the center.
Sets two contrasting elements against each other in the picture, such as light and dark halves, opposing colors, or characters from rival sides.
Poster artwork with a deliberate image or typography hierarchy, composed for its communication purpose. Text, credits, margins, and subject count vary with the design.
Lays out a top-down diagram of a room's desks or seats with a name or small face on each, showing who sits where.
Lays the picture out as a printed pencil board: a glossy rounded-corner rectangle carrying promotional character art edge to edge.
Splits the picture into gallery-style tiles with straight dividing lines or a four-point sparkle shape at the center, mimicking how stitched images sit in an online gallery grid.
Surrounds the subject with caption boxes of measurements, numbers, and labeled traits, like a character profile or data sheet.
Places two nearly identical side-by-side views of the same scene so they merge into a single image with depth when the eyes cross or relax.
Yields an extremely tall narrow picture, at least four times higher than wide, suited to a full standing figure or a stacked vertical scene.
Splits one cohesive picture into several separate images that only reassemble into the whole when tiled together as gallery thumbnails.
Adds thin crop marks at the four corners of the picture, short paired lines showing where a printed sheet would be cut to size.
Divides the picture into three upright panels set side by side, usually a larger central panel flanked by two narrower wings.
Lays the picture out to fit a round paddle fan, with the artwork shaped to the fan face and a handle or fastener hole cutting into the bottom edge.
Shows the same character repeated several times across the picture in different outfits, hairstyles, or color schemes for comparison.
Game-cover artwork organizing the principal image and any required title or platform information for its intended format.
Yields an extremely wide panoramic strip, at least four times wider than tall, suited to sweeping landscapes or a row of characters.
Frames the picture in a wide 16:9 or similar aspect ratio, like a modern monitor or film frame, with a broad horizontal field.
A single illustration laid out as an episode closing card, with a short caption or preview line and a staff credit in the corner.
A chapter-opening hero illustration with the title and a tagline laid over a striking full-page image of the lead character.
Lays out the stages of a drawing side by side, from rough sketch through lineart and flat color to the finished piece.
Polished key-visual artwork with the cast arranged in a showcase composition, a clean high-finish render, and often a title logo or blank space left for one.
A captured-screen presentation whose visible application, game or device interface follows the selected view. Window frames, cursors and status bars appear only when part of that view.
Joins several separate pictures edge to edge into one taller or wider image, the artwork continuing across the joins.
Yields the clean version of an illustration with all dialogue, titles, logos and rating marks removed, leaving only the artwork.
Magazine-cover layout with unreadable text; watch for invented titles resembling real magazines.

entries.term: album cover with artist and title
entries.description: Frames the picture as square music cover art with an artist name and title laid over the image and a clean square edge.

entries.term: cover page with title and author
entries.description: Frames the picture as the front cover of a book or magazine, with a title, author name, and other printed text over the art.

entries.term: doujin cover with circle name and content rating
entries.description: Frames the picture as the cover of a self-published comic, with a title, a circle name, and a content rating over the art.

entries.term: dvd cover with spine and disc logo
entries.description: Frames the picture as a home video sleeve, with a title, a spine, and a disc logo laid over the art in a tall rectangle.

entries.term: manga cover with title author and volume
entries.description: Frames the picture as the cover of a manga volume, with a large title logo, author name, and volume number over the art.
Makes the entire picture read as a printed poster, with a bold central image, title lettering, credits, and a designed layout with margins.

entries.term: video game cover with platform and rating marks
entries.description: Lays the picture out as game box art with a bold title logo, a platform banner, a rating badge, and a dramatic hero image.
A deliberate combination of distinct rendering or material treatments. Each treatment has a selected extent and role in the whole composition.
An arrangement of photographic fragments forming a selected association or constructed scene. Visible seams, shared space and scale depend on the intended construction.
A coordinated facing-page composition that organizes images, text and supporting material across a shared reading field.
A visual explanation that organizes supported information through pictures, diagrams, symbols, text and their meaningful relationships.
A static story screen coordinating a scene with any selected character display, dialogue area, speaker indication or choice interface.
A compact visual field pairing a recognizable subject or picture with selected labels, symbols or facts in a clear local hierarchy.

categories.name: Comic Symbols and Speech Bubbles
categories.description: Manga symbols drawn beside a character and the marks placed inside speech bubbles.

entries.description: A manga symbol of delight beside the character, three short lines on an arc; sometimes swaps with ^^^.
A drawn arrow pointing at something.
A black band framing the picture.
A speech balloon with no words in it.
A cross-shaped vein mark on the temple; anger as a drawn symbol.
A floating exclamation mark beside the head; surprise or alarm as a drawn symbol.
Short radiating lines around the head marking happiness; floating flowers for flowers instead.
Hearts floating beside the character, sometimes held as an object; heart background for a backdrop.
Several hearts floating around the head to mark infatuation; a single heart is heart or spoken heart.
The three-comma swirl emblem.
The three-line manga symbol of noticing something, with a matching expression.
A pink band framing the picture.
A small empty bubble marking a sigh.
A character relationship chart; too random to be useful.
Jagged three-line manga symbol of complaint; weak.
A comic told with no dialogue.
The spade shape from playing cards.
Plus-shaped sparkles around the head.
An anger mark inside a speech bubble, with a slightly annoyed expression.
Blush marks inside a speech bubble, with an embarrassed blushing face.
A speech bubble containing an ellipsis.
A speech bubble containing an exclamation mark, with a surprised look as a side effect.
A speech bubble containing a heart; very reliable.
A speech bubble containing an interrobang, with a surprised look as a side effect.
A speech bubble containing a musical note; the expression varies.
A speech bubble containing a question mark, with a puzzled look as a side effect.
The wavy sleepy-symbol beside a drowsy character, with a sleepy face.
A scribbled swirl beside the face marking displeasure, with a sulky expression; spoken squiggle puts it in a bubble.
A drawn star mark.
A feature drawn in the shape of a symbol.
The single comma-shaped swirl emblem.
Frames the picture with an elaborate decorative border of scrollwork, geometric motifs, or small figures running along its full length.
Rounds off the four corners of the picture's border into smooth curves instead of sharp right angles.

categories.name: Subject Count and Groups
categories.description: Terms that set how many subjects appear and how they are related.

entries.description: One male figure.
One male figure and one female figure.
One female; on illustrious-family models nearly the same as 1girl.
One female figure.
One man; nearly the same as 1boy.
One adult woman with a distinctly mature face on illustrious-family models.
One male; nearly the same as 1boy.
One adult man; on illustrious-family models nearly the same as 1boy.
One subject of unstated gender such as a robot, masked figure, mascot, or monster; describe it with other tags.
One adult woman; on some models the face reads older than 1girl.
Two male figures.
Two female figures.
Six or more, usually a crowd of ten or more; everyone is better for a group picture.
A mixed-gender sibling pair; reads well.
Two boys as brothers, often with matching hair and eyes; twins for identical.
Two characters in an intimate picture; often two women.
Many figures filling the space.
An uncountable crowd of women; crowd alone is mixed.
Two figures.
A group picture of five or more; characters tend to share attributes, and a face-fix pass is needed.
A family group; a count works.
A father with a daughter; unstable.
Several figures together.
A mother with a daughter who tends to be three or four; set the age if needed.
More than one male figure.
More than one female figure.
Two girls as sisters, often with matching hair and eyes; twins for identical.
One figure in the picture and no other.
Several characters are present, with the composition emphasizing one of them.
Objects only, no figure.
Three figures.
Identical twins; pair with 2girls or 2boys.
An elderly figure and a small child together as grandparent and grandchild, with no shared features.
An adult and a child together as parent and child, with no family resemblance between them.
Two young figures raised as siblings, side by side with no shared family features.
A figure and a far later descendant in one frame, generations apart but alike in the face.
A grown woman together with her sibling's young son.
A grown woman together with her sibling's young daughter.
A man and a woman together as family by marriage rather than by blood.
aliases: brother in law and sister in law

entries.description: Two men in frame together, related as brothers by marriage rather than blood.
Two or more young relatives of the same generation together, sharing a loose family resemblance.
A man together with his own child, the two sharing family features.
A man and his son together, the boy echoing the older face beside him.
An older man together with his son's wife, family by marriage rather than blood.
aliases: father in law and daughter in law

entries.description: An older man together with his daughter's husband, family by marriage rather than blood.
aliases: father in law and son in law

entries.description: An elderly man together with his young granddaughter.
An elderly man together with his young grandson.
An elderly woman together with her young granddaughter.
An elderly woman together with her young grandson.
A very old man together with his great-granddaughter, three generations between them.
A very old man together with his great-grandson, three generations between them.
Two siblings who share a single parent, alike in some features and unalike in others.
A woman together with her own child, usually held close or leaning against her.
A woman and her son together, the boy echoing her features.
An older woman together with her son's wife, family by marriage rather than blood.
aliases: mother in law and daughter in law

entries.description: An older woman together with her daughter's husband, family by marriage rather than blood.
aliases: mother in law and son in law

entries.description: An adult and their child together where neither reads specifically as a mother or a father.
Four siblings of one birth together, near identical in face and build.
Five siblings of one birth together, near identical in face and build.
Seven siblings of one birth together, near identical in face and build.
Six siblings of one birth together, near identical in face and build.
Two women in frame together, related as sisters by marriage rather than blood.
An adult together with their spouse's child, family without a shared resemblance.
Two young figures made siblings by their parents' marriage, with no shared features.
Three siblings of one birth together, near identical in face and build.
A grown man together with his sibling's young son.
A grown man together with his sibling's young daughter.
Two characters whose gender is left ambiguous or unreadable in the frame.
Three male characters in the frame, the count a three man group picture needs stated.
Three female characters in the frame, the count a three woman group picture needs stated.
Three characters whose gender is left ambiguous or unreadable in the frame.
Four male characters sharing the frame, the count a four man group picture needs stated.
Four female characters sharing the frame, the count a four woman group picture needs stated.
Four characters whose gender is left ambiguous or unreadable in the frame.
Five male characters sharing the frame, enough to crowd a group composition.
Five female characters sharing the frame, enough to crowd a group composition.
Five characters whose gender is left ambiguous or unreadable in the frame.
Six or more male characters filling the frame as a crowd.
Six or more characters of unreadable gender filling the frame as a crowd.
An enormous cast packed into one picture, dozens of figures filling every part of the frame.
Two or more identical copies of the same figure in one scene, matching face and outfit exactly.
Figures from unrelated worlds sharing one scene, their separate looks clashing side by side.
Two versions of the same figure together in one scene, alike in face but different in dress or age.
Two figures built to resemble each other closely, posed together so the likeness reads at a glance.
More than one dog in the frame, two or more of them sharing the scene.
Several characters whose gender is left ambiguous or unreadable, grouped in one frame.
Three or more versions of the same figure together in one scene, each styled differently.
Cats crowding the frame in uncountable numbers, at least half a dozen piled everywhere.

categories.name: Head and Hair Poses
categories.description: Poses of the head and actions performed on hair.

entries.description: Biting the own hair.
Braiding, usually a single braid; braiding another's hair for someone else's.
Brushing another character's hair; weak.
Brushing the own hair; weak.
Holding the hair up as if trying a style, often in a mirror-like framing.
Cheeks pulled sideways, by a POV hand unless stated.
Two characters pressing cheeks together; needs 2girls or couple, and negative cheek_bulge if the cheeks distort.
A puffed cheek; easily unnatural.
Squeezing the own cheeks, often turning the outline comic.
Cutting a lock of the own hair; weak.
Weight on the elbows on a desk or the ground, sometimes becoming head rest.
Glasses pushed up on the forehead, usually sunglasses.
Grabbing another character's hair.
The sweeping hair toss; weak alone, so pair with hair lift or hand in own hair.
A hand closes on hair.
Lifting a lock of hair; weak, and may lift clothing instead.
Hair pulled by a hand.
Doing hair: braiding, cutting, or brushing; own hair or another's hair sets whose.
A hand touching another figure's ear.
Both hands laid on another figure's face.
Both hands laid on one's own face.
The head lowered so the face is hidden, stronger than looking down.
The head held by a fistful of hair.
The chin resting on one or both hands.
The head raised in an upward glance, milder than looking up.
Freshly cut short hair with a rueful expression.
A kiss on another's hair or head; can become an ordinary kiss.
Fondly touching another character's hair.
Touching the own hair, a larger motion than twirling.
Fiddling with the own hair despite the wavy-hair reading.
Bringing the own hair to the nose, with a small white scent wisp; weak.
A hat worn at an angle.
Tucking hair behind the ear.
Tying hair, usually into a ponytail with a ribbon or tie held in the mouth; negative mouth hold if unwanted.
Hair whipping through the air from wind or a sharp turn.
A finger winding a lock of hair around itself beside the face, an idle nervous fidget.
A hand raised to the hair, smoothing or tucking a section back into place.
A brush or comb drawn down through the hair in long strokes.
Scissors closing on another figure's hair with cut strands falling away.
A length of hair pulled into the mouth and chewed between the teeth.
A strand of the figure's own hair caught and held between the lips.
A hand gathering another figure's hair, cradling the strands gently in the palm.
A hand lifting or gathering a length of the figure's own hair.
A tongue drawn slowly along a lock of another figure's hair.
Hair wound tight around a throat and pulled, the strands biting into the neck.
A pose with the head tipped laterally toward one shoulder.
A pose with the head rotated to one side relative to the torso.
A pose with the head and gaze directed upward.
A pose with the head and gaze directed downward.
A pose with the face directed straight ahead relative to the body.
A pose with the head angled just a little away from an upright position.
A pose with the head's weight supported by a hand beneath the chin, jaw, or side of the face.

categories.name: Leg and Foot Poses
categories.description: Poses and actions of the legs, feet, and toes.

entries.description: One knee bent.
Both knees bent.
Something placed between the legs.
The arms-up pick-me-up gesture; some models draw a small child being carried instead.
Ankles crossed in a poised stance; seated it drifts toward cross-legged, and contrapposto pairs well.
Toes curled under.
The foot flexed upward; weak alone.
Both feet raised, often the lying-on-front pose with feet kicking.
Kissing or licking another's feet.
Knees turned outward with the feet touching.
Knees drawn to the chest with the legs together; hugging own legs adds the arms.
Knees touching with the feet apart, the pigeon-toed girlish stance.
A leg lifted higher than leg up, sometimes held by hand.
One leg raised, a lively accent like knee up.
Standing with the legs spread in a bold stance, distinct from spread legs.
The legs folded back behind the head.
Both legs lifted, as when lying on the back.
Legs pressed together, standing or seated; the opposite of spread legs.
Both legs raised, in many situations including seen from above.
One leg raised, the other bearing the weight.
One leg extended; outstretched legs for both, folded_legs for the opposite.
Toes turned inward; negative pigeon if a bird appears.
The foot pointed so shin and foot align; negative plant or planter if plants appear.
A sole shown to the viewer suggestively, close up, with foreshortening.
One foot lifted clear of the ground, the leg mostly straight.
The heel lifted with the toes still down; mid-step or on tiptoe.
One leg lifted off the ground.
One paw lifted, hand or foot.
Toes spread; prone to distortion and extra toes.
A standing split with one leg straight up; add hold own leg or hug own leg to hold it.
A hero stance with a weapon thrust toward the camera in strong perspective.
Feet tickled with a feather or hand, with trembling; disembodied hand for a hand alone.
Toes curled tight.
Toes pointed toward the viewer; fails alone, pair with a pose tag.
Stepping on something, usually only the foot drawn.
Stepping on something; sometimes only the foot is drawn, so name the object.
Tying shoelaces; specify the shoes, posture, and angle.
Feet drawn with only the big toe outlined and the others merged, like the split shape of tabi socks.
Turns the bottoms of the feet toward the viewer, showing the arches, pads and toe creases.
Straightens and tenses both legs into a rigid line with the toes pointed sharply downward.
A pose with the legs opened wide apart, leaving clear space between the thighs.
A pose with one ankle crossed over or in front of the other while the legs remain close.
A pose with one leg crossing over the other at the thighs, knees, calves, or ankles.
A pose with the legs lifted above their usual resting position, often extending upward while reclining.
A pose with the knees flexed so the thighs and lower legs form angles.
A pose with the legs stretched out and the knees nearly or fully straightened.
A seated or elevated pose with the legs hanging freely without firm support beneath the feet.
A pose with both legs folded and gathered to one side of the body.

categories.name: First-Person and Viewer Interaction
categories.description: First-person framings and actions directed at the viewer or the camera.

entries.description: First-person view from a character in the scene; the viewer's hands or lower body may show. Lowercase pov works too.
An extremely crowded group picture; ill suited to generation.
A weapon aimed at the camera; pair with finger gun for the finger version.
A taunt toward the viewer; no effect alone.
An inviting gesture toward the viewer; no effect alone, use seductive smile and beckoning.
The subject eats food the viewer holds out; incoming food for the reverse.
The viewer is a woman, for feminine hands in frame.
Firing a gun at the camera with a muzzle flash; aiming at viewer only points it.
The subject hypnotizes the camera, with glow and spiral eyes.
An attack or attack stance toward the camera; pair with punching or kicking.
A drink held out to the camera.
Food held out to the camera, sometimes on a spoon; feeding for the third-person version.
A punch thrown at the camera.
The viewer pinned in a wall-slam; pov hand and wall tend to intrude, so negative them.
A crowd of girls, around eight.
First-person view of a subject lying on a bed looking back; bed invitation for an inviting mood.
First-person view across a table at a seated subject, often in head rest.
The subject shows affection toward the camera, a kiss-ready face or a hug.
The subject teases the camera; without an expression tag it lands as a flustered tsundere.
A first-person view past the own lower body, usually sexual; negative erection under clothes if a bulge appears.
A first-person date with the subject, with a date-like background.
The viewer's own hand entering the picture.
The viewer's hands in frame; pair with other pov tags, and female pov for a woman's hands.
Running at the camera with force.
The newlywed dinner-or-bath greeting; no effect alone, build it from naked apron, seductive smile, pov, holding ladle.
Sitting on someone's shoulders; unstable, shoulder carry is steadier.
The receiving partner's viewpoint; in safe content little different from pov.
A crowd of ten or more girls.
A view between spread legs, or the viewer's legs framing the subject.
The viewer's phone hand at the frame edge; pair with pov hands.
The subject holds a leash that runs to the camera.
Water droplets on the lens as in rain; hard, and against_glass may help.

categories.name: Content Rating
categories.description: Rating vocabulary that sets the content tier of a picture, usable in the positive or the negative.

entries.description: The explicit rating: genitals, penetration, ejaculation, and cut-ins become far more likely than with nsfw; negative penis or trembling when unwanted.
The all-ages rating; in the positive it removes adult mood, in the negative it strengthens it.
The mild adult rating; nipples begin to appear.
The all-ages rating in its colon form, which is part of the tag.
The mild adult rating in its colon form.
The sensitive rating in its colon form.
The sensitive rating: some exposure, nothing further.
The all-ages rating on the families whose rating terms name it safe rather than general, such as Anima.

categories.name: Visual registers
categories.description: Whole-look presets a series or a shot can adopt: each names the coverage scale, camera behaviour, light, colour, pacing, and finish that make a picture read as that kind of film, and the words that evoke it. Name the behaviour, not only the label; a label alone leaves the choices to the model.

entries.description: Shapes, colour, texture, and movement express the feeling without a story: macro detail, light play, particles, reflections, slow and rhythmic motion.

High-energy sequence cut to the theme: character run-ins, speed lines and impact flashes, dramatic cuts between scenes, poses held at peak tension, strong backlight and lens flare, a title card. One beat per clip.

Quiet observational anime: medium shots on a soft 35mm feel, tiny secondary motion (a sleeve in the wind, a snack bag crinkling), hand-painted sky gradients, warm rim light against cool shadow. Avoid action poses and glossy 3D.
Warm natural window light, cheerful pastel colour, medium-wide 28mm feel at eye level, simple motion gags. Avoid slapstick chaos, distortion, and dark dramatic lighting.

Film-like coverage: medium to close shots, one wide establishing shot per scene, camera moves motivated by action or a look, shallow focus, directional light with a colour grade. Write the behaviour (slow push-in, warm practical light, teal and orange grade) rather than the word alone, which leaves every choice to the model.
Close medium hero composition, slow luxury camera language (a slow arc, light sliding across a surface), soft edge light, material texture named. Avoid floating renders and sterile white backgrounds.

Observational look: shoulder-height handheld feel, slightly imperfect framing, natural fluorescent or window light, tactile ordinary motion (steam moves, a bowl is set down), honest and unposed. Avoid dramatic spotlights, product gloss, and fake film grain.
Typography carries the song: words appear on or beside the picture in time with the vocal, over simple animated backgrounds or slow abstract motion.

The page as film: variable panel sizes as shot sizes, a double-page spread as the wide shot, dramatic close-ups on faces, high-contrast black and white, screentone, speed and focus lines, impact frames, borderless panels for atmosphere.

A short story cut to the music: cinematic coverage of a beat that gives each scene a reason to exist, cutaways and B-roll for texture, colour keyed to the mood (warm gold, cold blue shadows, neon glow, or plain daylight).

The artist performs to camera: lip sync, direct address, cuts on the beat, whip pans and crash zooms, strobe or colour-wash lighting, slow motion on the chorus, wide then close alternation. The song's energy sets the camera speed.
Neutral eye-level coverage, available light, no grade beyond a slight warmth, motion only from the subjects; the register for evidence stills and continuity plates.
Clean 1970s future design, warm sunlight with a soft cyan glow, wide 35mm feel with a smooth slow push-in, hopeful mood. Avoid neon cyberpunk and dark dystopia.
Medium-wide 40mm feel, quiet symmetrical composition, warm practical light against soft blue street colour, tiny emotional changes (a look up, a step closer). Avoid posed romance and melodrama.
Cuts the piece like a music video: a performer or subject framed in rhythmic stylized shots, dramatic colored lighting, and quick changes of set and mood.

categories.name: Camera movement
categories.description: Moves of the camera body or lens for video prompts. Pair every move with a speed word or a duration, because models have no default speed; describe what each stage of a move reveals rather than stacking verbs; one move per shot is what most surfaces honour.

entries.description: The camera travels a curved path around the subject without completing a circle; subtle added motion.
The camera lifts high above the scene; establishing scale. Also drone rise.
An extremely fast zoom in or out; comedy and shock reveals.
The camera body moves closer; the background shifts in perspective. Also written push-in. Use for tension and emotion.
The camera body retreats; the environment expands around the subject. Also written pull-back or pull out. Use for reveals and endings.
The body dollies while the lens zooms the opposite way, so the subject holds size while the background stretches; vertigo.
Electronically stabilised motion, the smoothest, for complex paths.
Subtle natural shake and slightly imperfect framing; documentary realism.

The camera does not move at all. Reinforce it in prose (the camera is entirely motionless for the duration) and give the scene other motion, because a static frame is the hardest request for a video model.
The camera circles the subject completely; hero moments. Works on some surfaces only.
The camera swivels horizontally on a fixed position, without parallax; follows action or reveals what is beside the frame.
The camera swivels horizontally to the right on a fixed position.
The whole camera drops straight down.
The whole camera rises straight up.
Same as dolly out: the body travels backward.
Same as dolly in: the body travels forward, keeping perspective natural (a zoom does not).
The camera and framing hold while the focus shifts between planes; the cheapest way to redirect attention mid-shot.
Time slowed; the action plays at a fraction of its speed. Write which action is slowed and for how long.
A word such as slow, gentle, or fast, or a duration such as a five-second pan, attached to a camera move; without one the speed is arbitrary.
Stabilised handheld: smooth while walking, following without rawness.
The camera pivots vertically downward on a fixed position.
The camera pivots vertically upward on a fixed position; reveals height.
The camera follows a moving subject, keeping it in frame; name the direction it follows from.
The camera slides sideways to the left, parallel to the subject; walk-and-talks.
The camera slides sideways to the right, parallel to the subject.
A very fast pan that smears the frame into motion blur; an energetic transition between two views.
The lens focal length increases; the image flattens and the framing tightens without the body moving.
The lens focal length decreases; the framing widens without the body moving.

categories.name: Shot grammar
categories.description: The units and rules of coverage: what kind of shot a frame is within a scene, and the continuity rules between shots. These are planning words; most become framing terms or camera moves in the prompt itself.

entries.description: Keep the camera on one side of the axis between two characters so each stays on the same side of the frame across cuts; crossing it flips left and right.
The imaginary line between two interacting characters, or along a character's movement, that the 180-degree rule protects.
A contemplative pause with no camera or subject movement; a beat held before or after an action.
The set of shots gathered so a scene can be edited coherently: master, singles, over-the-shoulders, inserts, reactions.
An interruption of the main action with a view of something else, followed by a cut back.
Foreground, middle, and background all sharp.
A cut from a character looking to what they are looking at; the audience reads the second shot as what the first one sees.
A doorway, window, or arch inside the picture frames the subject.
A shot of part of the scene from a different angle or focal length than the master, emphasising a detail (hands, an object) already covered.
One shot that holds the whole dramatised scene from start to finish with every player in view; the geography the closer shots inherit.
A cut that joins two shots on a shared shape, motion, or position so the transition reads as one gesture.
A move that follows a character's action or look rather than moving on its own; the reason for the move is visible in the frame.
A single narrative moment per short clip; a second beat in the same clip competes with the first.
A cutaway to a participant reacting to what has just happened.
A shot from the opposite side of the previous one along the same axis; fixtures that were on the right stand on the left.
A narrow plane in focus and the rest soft.
A shot holding one person alone in a scene with others.
A shot holding two people; the distance between them is the content.

categories.name: Manga cinematics
categories.description: Devices from the manga page that image models draw as content: motion and emphasis marks, panel rhythm, and the page's equivalents of shot sizes.

entries.description: A panel whose boundary is implied by space or image edges rather than a drawn frame. Its effect depends on its content and relation to neighboring panels.
A composition spanning two facing pages. It can carry one large scene or several related views; the central binding affects placement.
A tight panel on a face or object to carry an emotional state or an important detail.
Lines radiating from a point to concentrate attention on it; also used for shock and emphasis.
A single bright element against deep black, or near-monochrome darkness with one bright accent.
A single high-contrast frame at the moment of impact, often black and white with radiating lines.
Dense cross-hatching used for shadow, texture, and tension in inked manga.
The pattern of panel extent, content density, repetition, and gaps across a sequence. These support emphasis and pacing together; panel size alone does not specify reading time.
Comic panels separated by plain gaps of empty space rather than drawn frame lines, giving the page an open airy layout.
A comic page whose panels and speech balloons read left to right, the reverse of the usual right to left manga order.
Orders the comic panels and speech balloons from right to left across the page, so the reading path runs opposite to a Western strip.
One wide narrative image spans two facing pages, with important details positioned in relation to the central binding.

categories.name: Camera phrases for prose video surfaces
categories.description: One-sentence camera descriptions in the prose a video surface reads. Each names the scale, the move, and what stays stable; swap the subject and keep the shape. Each entry is a whole phrase and reads as its own meaning.

entries.term: Aerial wide shot drifting forward slowly above the stable landscape
entries.description: A high, wide aerial view that glides slowly forward over a steady landscape, gradually bringing distant scenery closer while preserving the sense of scale.

entries.term: Balanced two subject medium shot with fixed spacing and stable focus
entries.description: A medium view of two subjects arranged with equal visual weight, holding their relative spacing and focus steady so their interaction remains clear.

entries.term: Centered close shot with locked focus and no visible camera shake
entries.description: A close, centered view with locked focus and a shake-free camera, keeping the subject's details steadily visible.

entries.term: Centered full body shot with a slight forward drift and level horizon
entries.description: A centered view of the entire body that drifts slightly closer while keeping the horizon level, adding gentle emphasis without disturbing the figure's alignment.

entries.term: Chest level close shot with a single controlled pullback after the action
entries.description: A chest-height close view that holds through the action, then pulls back once in a controlled move to reveal more of the subject and immediate surroundings.

entries.term: Close portrait framing with a barely perceptible handheld breathing motion
entries.description: A tight portrait with subtle handheld sway resembling breathing, giving the frame a gentle human presence while the face remains dominant.

entries.term: Close shot beginning on the hands then tilting once toward the face
entries.description: A close view that starts on the hands and makes one upward tilt to the face, connecting the hand action with the subject's expression.

entries.term: Close shot with one gentle tilt following the character downward movement
entries.description: A close view with one gentle downward tilt that follows the character's descent, keeping the moving subject framed.

entries.term: Exterior establishing shot with a gradual pan across the stable location
entries.description: A wide exterior view that slowly pans across a steady location, introducing its layout and spatial relationships before or during the action.

entries.term: Eye level medium shot with one smooth pullback revealing more environment
entries.description: An eye-level medium view that smoothly retreats once, making the subject smaller in frame and revealing more of the surrounding environment.

entries.term: Fixed close shot allowing expression and secondary movement to carry the scene
entries.description: A motionless close view that leaves room for facial expressions and small background or body movements to supply the scene's action.

entries.term: Fixed telephoto shot observing action from a distance without reframing
entries.description: A stationary, magnified view of distant action that holds its framing throughout, producing compressed depth and an observational feel.

entries.term: Foreground framed wide shot with a subtle sideways slide into clear view
entries.description: A wide view partly shaped by foreground elements that slides gently sideways, moving past the obstruction to give a clearer view of the scene.

entries.term: Front facing tracking shot moving backward smoothly as the character approaches
entries.description: A front-facing view that tracks smoothly backward ahead of an approaching character, preserving their size and frontal orientation as they advance.

entries.term: Full body tracking shot preserving feet hands and silhouette throughout motion
entries.description: A moving full-body view that follows the character while keeping the feet, hands, and entire silhouette inside the frame, making the motion easy to read.

entries.term: Gentle crane descent from an establishing view to character eye level
entries.description: A crane move that lowers smoothly from a broad establishing view to the character's eye level, shifting attention from the setting to the person.

entries.term: Gentle forward push from a medium shot while keeping the subject centered
entries.description: A medium view that moves slowly toward the centered subject, tightening the composition and increasing emphasis without changing the subject's position in frame.

entries.term: Gentle tilt down from the sky to reveal the complete scene below
entries.description: A camera tilt that begins on the sky and moves gently downward, revealing the full scene beneath it in one continuous motion.

entries.term: Ground level tracking shot moving beside the character feet and trailing fabric
entries.description: A ground-height tracking view moving alongside the character's feet and trailing fabric, emphasizing steps, motion, and the material sweeping behind.

entries.term: Grounded handheld medium shot with minimal sway and no sudden shake
entries.description: A handheld medium view with only slight natural sway and no abrupt shaking, giving the subject an immediate, grounded presence while staying readable.

entries.term: High angle close shot with fixed framing emphasizing quiet vulnerability
entries.description: A fixed close view looking down on the subject, using the elevated angle to make the figure appear quieter and more vulnerable.

entries.term: High angle wide shot with a slow controlled descent toward eye level
entries.description: A high, wide view that descends slowly and under control toward eye level, moving from an overview of the setting to a more direct encounter with the subject.

entries.term: High wide shot with a calm backward drift expanding the visible setting
entries.description: An elevated wide view that drifts calmly backward, expanding the visible setting and placing the subject within a broader spatial context.

entries.term: Intimate close shot with soft focus falloff and restrained forward movement
entries.description: A close, intimate view with gently blurred areas outside the focus plane and a slight forward move, concentrating attention on the subject's expression.

entries.term: Locked medium shot with stable framing and subtle natural subject movement
entries.description: A locked-off medium view with unchanging frame boundaries, allowing the subject's small natural movements to stand out against a stable composition.

entries.term: Long continuous take with smooth stabilization and no changes of camera axis
entries.description: An uninterrupted take with smooth camera stabilization and a fixed screen axis, preserving spatial orientation as the action unfolds.

entries.term: Long lens medium shot with compressed depth and controlled background motion
entries.description: A medium view through a long lens that compresses foreground and background depth while keeping background movement controlled, isolating the subject within a flattened space.

entries.term: Low angle close shot with a slow push emphasizing controlled determination
entries.description: A close view from below that pushes in slowly, making the subject appear more commanding and emphasizing a controlled, determined expression.

entries.term: Low angle medium shot with a restrained upward tilt toward the face
entries.description: A medium view from below that tilts upward slightly toward the face, shifting emphasis from the body to the expression while retaining the low-angle perspective.

entries.term: Low wide shot with a single forward glide close to the ground
entries.description: A wide view near ground level that makes one smooth forward glide, adding momentum while preserving the environment and the low perspective.

entries.term: Macro tracking shot following one small moving detail across the surface
entries.description: An extreme close-up that tracks a tiny moving detail across a surface, revealing fine texture and motion that would be lost in a wider view.

entries.term: Measured tilt up from the character hands toward the final facial expression
entries.description: A deliberate upward tilt from the character's hands to the face, ending on the resulting expression and linking the action to the reaction.

entries.term: Medium close shot with focus locked on the eyes throughout the movement
entries.description: A medium close view that keeps focus fixed on the eyes during movement, preserving their clarity and making the gaze the anchor of the shot.

entries.term: Medium close shot with shallow depth and a slow rack focus to the eyes
entries.description: A medium close view with a shallow focus range that shifts slowly onto the eyes, redirecting attention from the previous focal plane to the subject's gaze.

entries.term: Medium interior shot sliding slowly through the doorway toward the character
entries.description: A medium interior view that glides slowly through a doorway toward the character, using the threshold to reveal the room and create a sense of approach.

entries.term: Medium shot using a single slow zoom in without physical camera movement
entries.description: A stationary medium view whose lens zooms in slowly once, tightening the visible area and increasing emphasis without moving the camera closer.

entries.term: Medium shot using a single slow zoom out to reveal surrounding context
entries.description: A stationary medium view whose lens zooms out slowly once, widening the field of view to reveal context around the subject.

entries.term: Medium shot with a slow orbit ending on a balanced three quarter angle
entries.description: A medium view that orbits slowly around the subject and settles at a balanced three-quarter angle, revealing different sides and depth through the changing perspective.

entries.term: Medium shot with deep focus and a steady observational camera position
entries.description: A steady medium view with foreground and background kept clear in deep focus, presenting the subject and surroundings as an unobtrusive observed scene.

entries.term: Medium tracking shot circling one quarter turn around the moving character
entries.description: A medium tracking view that circles a quarter turn around a moving character, changing the visible side while following the action in one continuous move.

entries.term: Neutral eye level shot with documentary style stability and natural timing
entries.description: A level, eye-height view with steady documentary-style framing and unforced timing, presenting the action plainly without dramatic camera emphasis.

entries.term: One continuous camera move combining a gentle push with slight upward elevation
entries.description: A single uninterrupted camera move that pushes gently forward while rising slightly, bringing the subject closer as the viewpoint becomes a little higher.

entries.term: One continuous camera move combining side tracking with restrained forward drift
entries.description: A single uninterrupted move that tracks sideways while drifting slightly forward, following lateral action and gradually closing distance to the subject.

entries.term: Overhead static shot presenting clear movement paths across the ground
entries.description: A fixed view from directly above that shows routes across the ground clearly, turning the subjects' movement into readable paths and patterns.

entries.term: Overhead tracking shot following the character along one continuous route
entries.description: A directly overhead tracking view that follows the character along an uninterrupted route, preserving a clear map-like sense of direction and traveled space.

entries.term: Profile close shot tracking the face without changing the established scale
entries.description: A close side view that tracks with the face while maintaining its size in frame, keeping the profile and expression consistently prominent.

entries.term: Rear three quarter shot following the action with consistent spatial orientation
entries.description: A view from behind and to one side that follows the action while keeping directions consistent, showing both the character and what lies ahead without disorienting the viewer.

entries.term: Rear tracking shot following the character along the path at constant distance
entries.description: A tracking view behind the character that follows the path at an unchanging distance, keeping the figure's size steady and emphasizing forward travel.

entries.term: Shoulder level follow shot with smooth stabilization and natural walking rhythm
entries.description: A follow view at shoulder height with smooth stabilization and a subtle walking rhythm, keeping pace with the character while retaining a natural sense of movement.

entries.term: Side profile medium shot with a locked camera and passing background motion
entries.description: A fixed medium side view in which the subject's profile stays anchored while background elements pass through the frame, making motion visible around the stable composition.

entries.term: Single tracking shot maintaining screen direction throughout the complete action
entries.description: One continuous tracking shot that keeps movement in the same screen direction from beginning to end, preserving spatial clarity throughout the action.

entries.term: Slow crane rise from waist height to a broad view above the scene
entries.description: A crane move that rises slowly from waist height to an elevated wide view, progressively revealing the scene's layout and scale.

entries.term: Slow dolly left while the subject remains centered through coordinated framing
entries.description: A slow physical camera move to the left paired with coordinated framing that keeps the subject centered, shifting the background perspective around a stable focal point.

entries.term: Slow dolly right revealing new background detail without changing shot scale
entries.description: A slow physical camera move to the right that uncovers additional background detail while keeping the subject at the same size in frame.

entries.term: Slow lateral slide revealing the character from behind a foreground object
entries.description: A slow sideways camera slide that moves the view past a foreground object, gradually revealing the previously hidden character.

entries.term: Slow orbit around the stationary subject with consistent distance and horizon level
entries.description: A slow circular move around a motionless subject at constant distance and with a level horizon, revealing all sides without changing the subject's size or tilting the scene.

entries.term: Slow pan from the surrounding environment toward the waiting main subject
entries.description: A slow pan that travels from the surroundings to the waiting main subject, shifting attention from the location to the person without a cut.

entries.term: Slow retreat maintaining eye contact as the character advances toward camera
entries.description: A slow backward camera move that keeps an advancing character's gaze directed into the lens, sustaining eye contact and tension during the approach.

entries.term: Slow reveal from darkness into a centered medium shot without a cut
entries.description: A continuous reveal that emerges slowly from darkness into a centered medium view, introducing the subject without an edit.

entries.term: Smooth circular track keeping the subject centered through half an orbit
entries.description: A smooth circular tracking move that keeps the subject centered while traveling halfway around it, showing the opposite side with stable framing and changing background.

entries.term: Smooth point of view movement advancing carefully through the environment
entries.description: A stabilized point-of-view move that advances cautiously through the environment, showing the space from the mover's perspective and creating a careful sense of exploration.

entries.term: Smooth side tracking shot matching the character at a steady walking speed
entries.description: A smooth sideways tracking view moving at the character's walking speed, keeping pace with the figure while the background passes by.

entries.term: Stable medium shot with gradual focus shift from foreground to character
entries.description: A steady medium view in which focus shifts gradually from a foreground element to the character, transferring attention without moving the camera.

entries.term: Stable wide shot with gradual focus shift from character to distant environment
entries.description: A steady wide view in which focus shifts gradually from the character to the distant environment, drawing attention from the figure to the setting.

entries.term: Static macro shot focused on the object while hands move naturally around it
entries.description: A motionless extreme close-up of an object while hands move naturally around it, emphasizing fine detail and precise manual interaction.

entries.term: Static over shoulder framing directed toward the important object ahead
entries.description: A fixed view over a subject's shoulder toward the significant object beyond them, linking the observer and object within one composition.

entries.term: Static wide shot emphasizing environmental movement around the still character
entries.description: A motionless wide view that holds the character still within the frame while activity in the environment moves around them, emphasizing the contrast between stillness and motion.

entries.term: Steady diagonal approach from a wide shot toward medium character framing
entries.description: A stabilized camera approach along a diagonal path that changes a wide view into a medium framing of the character, combining closer emphasis with a shifting perspective.

entries.term: Three quarter medium shot with a gentle arc toward a frontal view
entries.description: A medium three-quarter view that arcs gently toward the front of the subject, gradually presenting a more frontal view while preserving shot scale.

entries.term: Tracking close shot maintaining facial focus during gentle character movement
entries.description: A close tracking view that keeps the face sharply focused as the character moves gently, preserving expression detail while following the motion.

entries.term: Tripod locked close shot with stable exposure and consistent facial proportions
entries.description: A tripod-fixed close view with unchanging framing and exposure, keeping facial proportions consistent so expression and detail can be compared without camera variation.

entries.term: Waist level medium shot with a gentle pan matching the character turn
entries.description: A waist-height medium view with a gentle pan that follows the character's turn, keeping the subject framed as their orientation changes.

entries.term: Wide angle follow shot preserving the environment around the moving subject
entries.description: A wide-angle follow view that stays with the moving subject while retaining substantial surrounding environment, emphasizing both movement and spatial context.

entries.term: Wide establishing shot followed by one gradual push toward the main subject
entries.description: A broad establishing view followed by one gradual push toward the main subject, moving attention from the overall location to the person within it.

entries.term: Wide interior shot with fixed perspective and carefully preserved room geometry
entries.description: A fixed wide interior view that keeps straight lines and room proportions stable, presenting the space and action without changing the spatial relationships.

entries.term: Wide landscape composition with the subject small and the camera completely locked
entries.description: A completely locked wide landscape composition that makes the subject small within the scenery, emphasizing environmental scale and the figure's place within it.

entries.term: Wide shot beginning on the environment then panning once toward the action
entries.description: A wide view that starts on the environment and makes one pan toward the action, connecting the setting to the event in a single continuous movement.

entries.term: Wide shot from behind the subject with a gradual rise over the shoulders
entries.description: A wide rear view that rises gradually until it looks over the subject's shoulders, revealing more of the space ahead while maintaining the subject's relationship to it.

entries.term: Wide shot with a slow push that ends before reaching medium framing
entries.description: A wide view that pushes in slowly but stops while still wide, adding modest emphasis to the subject without reaching medium framing.

entries.term: Wide symmetrical framing with a fixed camera and stable architectural lines
entries.description: A fixed, symmetrically composed wide view with steady architectural lines, producing a balanced, orderly image that emphasizes the structure of the space.

categories.name: Action phrases for prose video surfaces
categories.description: One-sentence character actions with a beginning, a middle, and an end, in the prose a video surface reads. Replace the character and the object. Each entry is a whole phrase and reads as its own meaning.

entries.term: The character adjusts the cloak against the wind then continues walking with purpose
entries.description: Shows the character securing a windblown cloak, then striding forward with renewed purpose, with the fabric settling into the walking motion.

entries.term: The character approaches the sleeping animal crouches nearby and waits without touching it
entries.description: Shows the character cautiously approaching and crouching beside a sleeping animal, then waiting quietly without making contact, creating a restrained moment of observation.

entries.term: The character balances on the narrow beam then jumps safely onto solid ground
entries.description: Shows the character balancing along a narrow beam before jumping to solid ground and landing safely, creating a clear transition from tension to stability.

entries.term: The character brushes dust from the surface before revealing a hidden engraved symbol
entries.description: Shows the character brushing dust away from a surface to uncover a hidden engraved symbol, turning obscured detail into a visible discovery.

entries.term: The character catches a drifting petal between two fingers then releases it again
entries.description: Shows the character catching a drifting petal between two fingers and then letting it float free, emphasizing delicate control and gentle motion.

entries.term: The character catches a falling object and holds it securely against the chest
entries.description: Shows the character intercepting a falling object and drawing it securely against the chest, ending its fall in a protective hold.

entries.term: The character catches the companion gently and sets it safely back on the ground
entries.description: Shows the character catching a companion and lowering them safely to the ground, turning a sudden rescue into a stable, gentle landing.

entries.term: The character catches the hat in the wind and secures it with both hands
entries.description: Shows the character snatching a windblown hat and pinning it down with both hands, stopping its flight and securing it against the wind.

entries.term: The character checks the injured hand wraps it carefully and resumes the task
entries.description: Shows the character checking an injured hand, wrapping it carefully, and returning to the task, moving from discomfort to a careful recovery.

entries.term: The character climbs the final steps and pauses to take in the wide landscape
entries.description: Shows the character completing a climb and stopping to survey the wide landscape, opening the action into a broad scenic reveal.

entries.term: The character closes both eyes breathes slowly and opens them with renewed confidence
entries.description: Shows the character closing both eyes, breathing slowly, and reopening them with renewed confidence, creating a visible shift from tension to composure.

entries.term: The character closes the workshop shutters extinguishes the lamp and walks toward the door
entries.description: Shows the character closing workshop shutters, putting out the lamp, and walking toward the door, darkening and quieting the space as work ends.

entries.term: The character crosses the room while trailing fingers lightly along the wooden table
entries.description: Shows the character crossing the room while lightly trailing their fingers along a wooden table, adding continuous tactile motion to the walk.

entries.term: The character dodges the first swing pivots aside and ends outside striking distance
entries.description: Shows the character evading an incoming swing, pivoting aside, and finishing beyond the attacker's reach, producing a compact defensive evasion.

entries.term: The character draws a glowing line through the air and completes a circular symbol
entries.description: Shows the character tracing a glowing line through the air until it forms a complete circular symbol, leaving a luminous shape suspended in the scene.

entries.term: The character draws a sword smoothly then settles into a controlled defensive guard
entries.description: Shows the character smoothly drawing a sword and settling into a controlled defensive guard, ending in a ready, stable combat posture.

entries.term: The character enters the rain then opens an umbrella with one smooth motion
entries.description: Shows the character stepping into the rain and opening an umbrella in one smooth motion, changing exposed rainfall into sheltered movement.

entries.term: The character enters the shallow water and moves forward against the gentle current
entries.description: Shows the character wading into shallow water and pushing forward against a gentle current, with resistance visible in the pace and surrounding ripples.

entries.term: The character follows a drifting light through the scene while keeping a steady pace
entries.description: Shows the character following a drifting light at a steady pace, creating continuous forward movement guided through the scene by the glow.

entries.term: The character follows the bird with the eyes before walking in the same direction
entries.description: Shows the character visually tracking a bird and then walking after it, turning a moment of attention into purposeful movement.

entries.term: The character follows the footprints then stops when they abruptly disappear
entries.description: Shows the character following a trail of footprints and stopping when it abruptly ends, shifting the motion into a moment of mystery.

entries.term: The character gathers the scattered papers while the wind continues pulling at their edges
entries.description: Shows the character gathering scattered papers while the wind keeps tugging at their edges, combining recovery of the pages with continuing fluttering motion.

entries.term: The character glances over one shoulder then pivots fully toward an approaching sound
